  intro h
  apply inv_not_continuousAt_zero
  have h1s : (1 : ℂ) - (0 : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by norm_num
  have heq : (fun s : ℂ => 1 / s)
      = fun s => completedRiemannZeta₀ s - 1 / (1 - s) - completedRiemannZeta s := by

/-! ### §2 The wall: the functional equation is the only reflection of `Λ` -/

/-- **The reflection rigidity of the completed zeta, unconditional.**  Any reflection
`s ↦ b − s` under which `Λ = completedRiemannZeta` is invariant has `b = 1`: it is the functional
equation `Λ(1 − s) = Λ(s)`, whose fixed point `b/2 = 1/2` lies on the critical line.

The reflection carries the pole at `0` to `b` and the pole at `1` to `b − 1`; `Λ` is continuous off
`{0, 1}`, so both images lie in `{0, 1}`, forcing `b = 1`.  No growth or transcendence input is
needed — the finiteness of the pole set does all the work. -/

source_arguments.name: RHTower.signedBernoulliMobiusResponse_insert
source_arguments.statement:
theorem signedBernoulliMobiusResponse_insert {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {p : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (hp : p ∉ s) (θ : ℕ → R)
    (response : Finset ℕ → R) :
    signedBernoulliMobiusResponse (insert p s) θ response =
      signedBernoulliMobiusResponse s θ response -
        θ p * signedBernoulliMobiusResponse s θ
          (fun t => response (insert p t))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem signedBernoulliMobiusResponse_insert {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
    {p : ℕ} {s : Finset ℕ} (hp : p ∉ s) (θ : ℕ → R)
    (response : Finset ℕ → R) :
    signedBernoulliMobiusResponse (insert p s) θ response =
      signedBernoulliMobiusResponse s θ response -
        θ p * signedBernoulliMobiusResponse s θ
          (fun t => response (insert p t))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  classical
  unfold signedBernoulliMobiusResponse
  rw [Finset.sum_powerset_insert hp, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  calc
    (∑ t ∈ s.powerset,
        ((-1 : R) ^ t.card * completeAliasWeight (insert p s) t θ *
              booleanMobiusResponse t response +
          (-1 : R) ^ (insert p t).card *
              completeAliasWeight (insert p s) (insert p t) θ *
                booleanMobiusResponse (insert p t) response)) =
        ∑ t ∈ s.powerset,
          (((-1 : R) ^ t.card * completeAliasWeight s t θ *
              booleanMobiusResponse t response) -
            θ p * ((-1 : R) ^ t.card * completeAliasWeight s t θ *
              booleanMobiusResponse t (fun u => response (insert p u)))) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro t ht
      have hts : t ⊆ s := Finset.mem_powerset.mp ht
      have hpt : p ∉ t := fun hmem => hp (hts hmem)
      rw [completeAliasWeight_insert_inactive hp hts,
        completeAliasWeight_insert_active hp hts,
        booleanMobiusResponse_insert hpt response,
        Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hpt, pow_succ]
      ring
    _ =
        (∑ t ∈ s.powerset,
          (-1 : R) ^ t.card * completeAliasWeight s t θ *
            booleanMobiusResponse t response) -
          θ p *
            ∑ t ∈ s.powerset,
              (-1 : R) ^ t.card * completeAliasWeight s t θ *
                booleanMobiusResponse t (fun u => response (insert p u)) := by
      rw [Finset.sum_sub_distrib, Finset.mul_sum]

/-- The collapsed signed occupancy response obeys the same deletion-contraction recursion. -/

theorem polarSinh_adjacent_eq_alpha_beta
    (x L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) :
    (∫ h in Ioc (x - L) x, 4 * Real.sinh (h / 2)) -
      (∫ h in Ioc (x - 2 * L) (x - L), 4 * Real.sinh (h / 2)) =
        4 * rectangularPolarAlpha L ^ 2 * Real.exp (x / 2) +
          4 * rectangularPolarBeta L ^ 2 * Real.exp (-x / 2)
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem polarSinh_adjacent_eq_alpha_beta
    (x L : ℝ) (hL : 0 ≤ L) :
    (∫ h in Ioc (x - L) x, 4 * Real.sinh (h / 2)) -
      (∫ h in Ioc (x - 2 * L) (x - L), 4 * Real.sinh (h / 2)) =
        4 * rectangularPolarAlpha L ^ 2 * Real.exp (x / 2) +
          4 * rectangularPolarBeta L ^ 2 * Real.exp (-x / 2)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le (by linarith : x - L ≤ x),
    ← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le (by linarith : x - 2 * L ≤ x - L)]
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul,
    intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul,
    intervalIntegral_sinh_half,
    intervalIntegral_sinh_half]
  rw [Real.cosh_eq, Real.cosh_eq, Real.cosh_eq,
    rectangularPolarAlpha, rectangularPolarBeta]
  have h1 : Real.exp ((x - L) / 2) =
      Real.exp (x / 2) * Real.exp (-L / 2) := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have h2 : Real.exp (-((x - L) / 2)) =
      Real.exp (-x / 2) * Real.exp (L / 2) := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have h3 : Real.exp ((x - 2 * L) / 2) =
      Real.exp (x / 2) * Real.exp (-L / 2) ^ 2 := by
    rw [pow_two, ← Real.exp_add, ← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  have h4 : Real.exp (-((x - 2 * L) / 2)) =
      Real.exp (-x / 2) * Real.exp (L / 2) ^ 2 := by
    rw [pow_two, ← Real.exp_add, ← Real.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  rw [h1, h2, h3, h4]
  ring

theorem integral_weighted_primeDensity (g : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (primeDensity g t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 - (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 + (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log s) +
      (Complex.log (s + 1 / 3) - Complex.log s)

theorem integral_weighted_primeDensity (g : ℝ) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (primeDensity g t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 - (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
      (Complex.log (s - 2 / 3 + (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) - Complex.log s) +
      (Complex.log (s + 1 / 3) - Complex.log s)
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  obtain ⟨h1, h0, hm, hp, ha⟩ := positive_rates g hs
  rw [setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi (fun t ht => weighted_primeDensity_split g s ht)]
  unfold frullaniKernel
  have h12 : IntegrableOn (fun t : ℝ =>
      (Complex.exp (-((s - 1) * t)) - Complex.exp (-((s - 2 / 3 - (g : ℂ) * Complex.I) * t))) / t +

      (Ioi 0) := (integrableOn_frullani h1 hm).add (integrableOn_frullani h0 hp)
  rw [integral_add h12 (integrableOn_frullani h0 ha), integral_add (integrableOn_frullani h1 hm)
    (integrableOn_frullani h0 hp), integral_frullani h1 hm, integral_frullani h0 hp,
    integral_frullani h0 ha]

source_arguments.statement:
theorem integral_cexp_mul_regularDensity {β γ δ : ℝ} (A : ℕ)
    (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hβ1 : β < 1) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (regularDensity β γ δ A t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) - (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
        ((Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))) +
          ((A : ℂ) - 1) * (Complex.log s - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem integral_cexp_mul_regularDensity {β γ δ : ℝ} (A : ℕ)
    (hδ1 : δ < 1) (hβ1 : β < 1) {s : ℂ} (hs : 1 < s.re) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (regularDensity β γ δ A t : ℂ)) =
      (Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) - (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - 1)) +
        ((Complex.log (s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))) +
          ((A : ℂ) - 1) * (Complex.log s - Complex.log (s - (δ : ℂ))))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have h1 : 0 < (s - (1 : ℂ)).re := by
    simpa using re_pos_of_one_lt (a := 1) le_rfl hs
  have hδ : 0 < (s - (δ : ℂ)).re := re_pos_of_one_lt hδ1.le hs
  have h0 : 0 < s.re := lt_trans one_pos hs
  obtain ⟨hm, hp⟩ := re_pos_sub_conj (β := β) (γ := γ) hβ1 hs
  have hsplit :
      (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), Complex.exp (-(s * t)) * (regularDensity β γ δ A t : ℂ)) =
        ∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
          ((Complex.exp (-((s - 1) * t)) - Complex.exp (-((s - β - γ * I) * t))) / t +
          ((Complex.exp (-((s - δ) * t)) - Complex.exp (-((s - β + γ * I) * t))) / t +
            ((A : ℂ) - 1) *
              ((Complex.exp (-((s - δ) * t)) - Complex.exp (-(s * t))) / t))) := by
    refine setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi ?_
    intro t ht
    exact cexp_mul_regularDensity β γ δ A s ht
  have hint3 : IntegrableOn
      (fun t : ℝ => ((A : ℂ) - 1) *
        ((Complex.exp (-((s - (δ : ℂ)) * t)) - Complex.exp (-(s * t))) / t)) (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) := by
    have := integrableOn_frullani hδ h0
    exact this.const_mul _
  have hint2 : IntegrableOn
      (fun t : ℝ => (Complex.exp (-((s - (δ : ℂ)) * t)) -
          Complex.exp (-((s - (β : ℂ) + (γ : ℂ) * I) * t))) / t +
        ((A : ℂ) - 1) *
          ((Complex.exp (-((s - (δ : ℂ)) * t)) - Complex.exp (-(s * t))) / t))
      (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) := (integrableOn_frullani hδ hp).add hint3
  rw [hsplit, integral_add (integrableOn_frullani h1 hm) hint2,
    integral_add (integrableOn_frullani hδ hp) hint3,
    integral_const_mul, integral_frullani h1 hm, integral_frullani hδ hp,
    integral_frullani hδ h0]

source_arguments.statement:
theorem integral_dampedFrullani {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t)
      = Real.log (Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 + 1))
source_arguments.source_statement:
theorem integral_dampedFrullani {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ), (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t)
      = Real.log (Real.sqrt (ε ^ 2 + 1))
source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hare : (0 : ℝ) < (1 : ℂ).re := by simp
  have hbre : (0 : ℝ) < ((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I).re := by
    simp only [Complex.sub_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.I_re, sub_zero]
    exact hε
  have hfr := integral_frullani hare hbre
  have hint := integrableOn_frullani hare hbre
  have hcomm := Complex.reCLM.integral_comp_comm hint
  simp only [Complex.reCLM_apply] at hcomm
  have hre : ∀ t ∈ Ioi (0 : ℝ),
      ((Complex.exp (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ))) - Complex.exp (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ))))
        / (t : ℂ)).re
        = (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t := by
    intro t ht
    have hr : (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ))).re = -(ε * t) := by
      simp only [Complex.neg_re, Complex.mul_re, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im,
        Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im]
      ring
    have him : (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ))).im = t := by
      simp only [Complex.neg_im, Complex.mul_im, Complex.sub_re, Complex.sub_im,
        Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, Complex.I_re, Complex.I_im]
      ring
    have h1 : (Complex.exp (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ)))).re = Real.exp (-t) := by
      rw [show (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ))) = ((-t : ℝ) : ℂ) from by push_cast; ring,
        ← Complex.ofReal_exp, Complex.ofReal_re]
    have h2 : (Complex.exp (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ)))).re
        = Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t := by
      rw [Complex.exp_re, hr, him]
    rw [div_ofReal_re, Complex.sub_re, h1, h2]
  have hleft : (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
      (Real.exp (-t) - Real.exp (-(ε * t)) * Real.cos t) / t)
      = (∫ t in Ioi (0 : ℝ),
          (Complex.exp (-((1 : ℂ) * (t : ℂ)))
            - Complex.exp (-(((ε : ℂ) - Complex.I) * (t : ℂ)))) / (t : ℂ)).re := by
    rw [← hcomm]
    exact (MeasureTheory.setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Ioi hre).symm
  rw [hleft, hfr, Complex.log_one, sub_zero, Complex.log_re]
  congr 1
  rw [Complex.norm_eq_sqrt_sq_add_sq]
  simp

\[
  \begin{pmatrix}P&R\\S&Q\end{pmatrix}^{-1}

    G+GRHSG&-GRH\\
    -HSG&H
  \end{pmatrix}
\]

\[
  PG=GP=1,\qquad KH=HK=1.
\]

It then proves the exact endpoint-dressed inverse contrast

\[
\begin{aligned}
  &B^{-1}QA^{-1}
  -B^{-1}(Q-SGR)A^{-1}\\
  &\qquad=(B^{-1}S)G(RA^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\]

private theorem physicalScalar_S (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : UpperHalfPlane) :
    scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates (S • z)) =
      scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates z) := by
  have h := physicalScalar_invert q ⟨z.re,z.im,z.im_pos⟩
  rw [UpperHalfPlane.modular_S_smul]
  simpa [coordinates,d4BMEisensteinInvertCoordinate,
    Complex.inv_re,Complex.inv_im,Complex.normSq_apply,sq,neg_div] using h

private theorem physicalScalar_T (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : UpperHalfPlane) :
    scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates (T • z)) =
      scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates z) := by
  simp only [coordinates,ModularGroup.re_T_smul,ModularGroup.im_T_smul]
  simpa [scalar] using
    d4BM_completedEisensteinCuspLeg_scalar_periodic (physicalAngularParameter q) z.im z.re

/-- The complete physical scattering field is invariant under the entire integral modular group. -/
theorem physicalScalar_modular (q : XiZeroCopy) (A : SL(2, ℤ)) (z : UpperHalfPlane) :
    scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates (A • z)) =
      scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates z) := by
  have hA : A ∈ Subgroup.closure {S,T} := by simp [SpecialLinearGroup.SL2Z_generators]
  suffices ∀ z : UpperHalfPlane, scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates (A • z)) =
      scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) (coordinates z) from this z
  induction hA using Subgroup.closure_induction with
  | mem g hg =>
    simp only [mem_insert_iff,mem_singleton_iff] at hg
    rcases hg with rfl | rfl
    · exact physicalScalar_S q
    · exact physicalScalar_T q
  | one => intro w; simp
  | mul g h _ _ ig ih => intro w; rw [mul_smul,ig,ih]
  | inv g _ ig => intro w; simpa using (ig (g⁻¹ • w)).symm

/-- The original linear field minus its complete smooth cusp principal subtraction. -/
def residual (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) : ℂ :=
  scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) z - cutoff z*principal (physicalAngularParameter q) z

/-- Below the cutoff the original source is retained literally. -/
theorem residual_low (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) (hz : z 1 ≤ 2) :
    residual q z = scalar (physicalAngularParameter q) z := by
  unfold residual cutoff
  rw [Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos (by linarith)]
  simp

/-- Above the cutoff every nonconstant Fourier mode remains, with its original normalization. -/
theorem residual_high (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) (hz : 3 ≤ z 1) :
    residual q z = tail (physicalAngularParameter q) z := by
  unfold residual cutoff
  rw [Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le (by linarith)]
  dsimp [scalar,D4BMGlobalAngularResponse.principal,tail,d4BMCompletedEisensteinCuspLeg]
  ring

/-- Integer translations preserve the literal cusp-subtracted source. -/
theorem residual_translate (q : XiZeroCopy) (n : ℤ) (z : UpperHalfPlane) :
    residual q (coordinates (T^n • z)) = residual q (coordinates z) := by
  simp only [residual,physicalScalar_modular]
  congr 1
  simp only [cutoff,D4BMGlobalAngularResponse.principal,d4BMCompletedEisensteinCuspConstantPart,
    d4BMCompletedEisensteinCuspConstantTerm,d4BMCompletedEisensteinCuspConstantMaassFactor,
    coordinates,ModularGroup.im_T_zpow_smul]
  rfl

/-- Full source germs agree across every closed-cell overlap, including the elliptic corners. -/
theorem residual_cell_compatible (q : XiZeroCopy) :

  intro γ z hz hγ
  induction γ using QuotientGroup.induction_on with

    by_cases hc : A 1 0 = 0
    · obtain ⟨n,hn⟩ := exists_eq_T_zpow_of_c_eq_zero hc
      apply Filter.Eventually.of_forall
      intro w
      dsimp only
      rw [hn]
      exact residual_translate q n w
    · obtain ⟨hl,hr⟩ := nonparabolic_cell_overlap_low A hc z hz hγ
      have hleft : ∀ᶠ w : UpperHalfPlane in 𝓝 z, w.im < 2 :=

ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq (centralSoninExteriorOverlap a) =

/-- The complete zero-mode-corrected Sonin projection energy is exactly twice the ordinary

theorem hsNormSq_centralSoninProjectionCorrection_eq_two_mul_timeBand

/-- The zero-mode-subtracted exterior overlap carries the same exact area `4 a²`. -/
theorem hsNormSq_centralSoninExteriorOverlap_eq_four_mul_sq

/-- The complete Sonin projection correction has exact Hilbert--Schmidt energy `8 a²`. -/
theorem hsNormSq_centralSoninProjectionCorrection_eq_eight_mul_sq

    ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq (centralSoninProjectionCorrection a) = 8 * a ^ 2 := by

/-- The exact principal-subtracted ambient Sonin dilation residual is Hilbert--Schmidt. -/
theorem centralSoninDilationCornerResidual_isHilbertSchmidt
    (a p : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hp : 1 < p) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.IsHilbertSchmidt (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp) :=
  (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual_mem_timeBandIdeal a p ha hp).isHilbertSchmidt

/-- **Uniform scale-independent residual bound.** The Hilbert--Schmidt energy of the exact
principal-subtracted Sonin dilation residual is controlled solely by the fixed projection
correction.  In particular, the bound does not grow with the dilation scale `p`. -/
theorem centralSoninDilationCornerResidual_hsNormSq_le
    (a p : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hp : 1 < p) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq (centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp) ≤
      16 * ContinuousLinearMap.hsNormSq (centralSoninProjectionCorrection a) := by
  open ContinuousLinearMap in
    let Q := centralSoninProjection a
    let Q₀ := centralSoninFormalComplement a
    let D := dilationSum p hp
    let C := centralSoninProjectionCorrection a
    let A : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2 := (1 - Q) * D * C
    let B : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2 := C * D * Q₀
    have hC : IsHilbertSchmidt C := by
      simpa [C] using centralSoninProjectionCorrection_isHilbertSchmidt a ha
    have hA : IsHilbertSchmidt A := by
      exact hC.comp_left ((1 - Q) * D)
    have hB : IsHilbertSchmidt B := by
      exact hC.comp_right (D * Q₀)
    have hEq : centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp = A - B := by
      change centralSoninDilationCornerResidual a p hp =
        (1 - Q) * D * C - C * D * Q₀
      simpa [Q, Q₀, D, C] using
        centralSoninDilationCornerResidual_eq_correction_factorization a p hp
    have hQ : ‖(1 : SoninL2 →L[ℂ] SoninL2) - Q‖ ≤ 1 := by
      simpa [Q] using norm_one_sub_centralSoninProjection_le_one a
    have hQ₀ : ‖Q₀‖ ≤ 1 := by
      simpa [Q₀] using norm_centralSoninFormalComplement_le_one a
    have hD : ‖D‖ ≤ 2 := by
      dsimp [D]
      apply (dilationSum p hp).opNorm_le_bound (by norm_num)
      intro f
      rw [dilationSum_apply]
      calc
        ‖dilation p (zero_lt_one.trans hp) f +
            dilation p⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hp)) f‖
            ≤ ‖dilation p (zero_lt_one.trans hp) f‖ +
              ‖dilation p⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hp)) f‖ := norm_add_le _ _
        _ = 2 * ‖f‖ := by
          rw [(dilation p (zero_lt_one.trans hp)).norm_map,
            (dilation p⁻¹ (inv_pos.mpr (zero_lt_one.trans hp))).norm_map]
          ring
    have hLD : ‖(1 - Q) * D‖ ≤ 2 := by
      calc
        ‖(1 - Q) * D‖ ≤ ‖1 - Q‖ * ‖D‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
        _ ≤ 1 * 2 := mul_le_mul hQ hD (norm_nonneg _) (by norm_num)
        _ = 2 := by norm_num
    have hDQ₀ : ‖D * Q₀‖ ≤ 2 := by
      calc
        ‖D * Q₀‖ ≤ ‖D‖ * ‖Q₀‖ := norm_mul_le _ _
        _ ≤ 2 * 1 := mul_le_mul hD hQ₀ (norm_nonneg _) (by norm_num)
        _ = 2 := by norm_num
    have hAbound : hsNormSq A ≤ 4 * hsNormSq C := by
      calc
        hsNormSq A ≤ ‖(1 - Q) * D‖ ^ 2 * hsNormSq C :=
          hsNormSq_comp_left_le hC ((1 - Q) * D)
        _ ≤ 4 * hsNormSq C := by
          apply mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right _ (hsNormSq_nonneg C)
          nlinarith [norm_nonneg ((1 - Q) * D)]

/-- The full three-term squared principal part, retaining both original Weyl coefficients. -/
def principalSquare (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) : ℂ := (principal (center q) z)^2/2

def squareResidual (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) : ℂ :=
  fullSquarePotential q z-cutoff z*principalSquare q z

/-- A continuous cusp-bounded coordinate field belongs to the actual quotient L² space. -/
theorem cuspBound_memLp (f : (Fin 2 → ℝ) → ℂ) (hf : ContinuousOn f domain)
    (B : ℝ) (hb : ∀ z, 3 < z 1 → ‖f z‖ ≤ B) :
    MemLp (fun z : UpperHalfPlane => f (coordinates z)) 2 D4BMModularCore.measure := by
  let lo : Fin 2 → ℝ := ![-1/2,1/2]
  let hi : Fin 2 → ℝ := ![1/2,4]
  have hc : ContinuousOn f (Icc lo hi) := hf.mono (by
    intro z hz
    have hh := hz.1 1
    change (1/2:ℝ) ≤ z 1 at hh
    change 0 < z 1
    linarith)
  obtain ⟨C,hC⟩ := isCompact_Icc.exists_bound_of_continuousOn hc
  have hcoordinates : Continuous coordinates := by
    apply continuous_pi
    intro i
    fin_cases i
    · exact UpperHalfPlane.continuous_re
    · exact UpperHalfPlane.continuous_im
  have hfc : Continuous (fun z : UpperHalfPlane => f (coordinates z)) :=
    hf.comp_continuous hcoordinates (fun z => z.im_pos)
  apply MemLp.of_bound hfc.aestronglyMeasurable (max C B)
  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem ModularGroup.isClosed_fd.measurableSet] with z hz
  have hre := abs_le.mp hz.2
  have hsq := ModularGroup.three_le_four_mul_im_sq_of_mem_fd hz
  have him : (1/2:ℝ) ≤ z.im := by nlinarith [z.im_pos]
  by_cases hh : 4 ≤ z.im
  · exact (hb (coordinates z) (by change 3 < z.im; linarith)).trans (le_max_right _ _)
  · apply (hC (coordinates z) ?_).trans (le_max_left _ _)
    constructor
    · intro i
      fin_cases i
      · simpa [lo,coordinates,neg_div] using hre.1
      · exact him
    · intro i
      fin_cases i
      · exact hre.2
      · exact le_of_not_ge hh

/-- Smooth cusp cutoff in the original chart. -/
theorem sourceCutoff_smooth : ContDiff ℝ ∞ cutoff := by
  let Y : (Fin 2 → ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℝ := ContinuousLinearMap.proj 1
  exact Complex.ofRealCLM.contDiff.comp (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff.comp
    (Y.contDiff.sub contDiff_const))

/-- The complete principal half-square is smooth on every positive-height chart. -/
theorem principalSquare_smooth (q : XiZeroCopy) : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (principalSquare q) domain :=
  ((cuspConstantPart_contDiffOn .scalar (center q)).pow 2).div_const 2

theorem squareResidual_continuousOn (q : XiZeroCopy) : ContinuousOn (squareResidual q) domain := by
  have hQ : ContinuousOn (fullSquarePotential q) domain :=
    fun z hz => (fullSquarePotential_smooth q z hz 0).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt
  exact hQ.sub (sourceCutoff_smooth.continuous.continuousOn.mul (principalSquare_smooth q).continuousOn)

/-- In the cusp this is precisely half of the complete scalar-square remainder, including every cross term. -/
theorem squareResidual_high (q : XiZeroCopy) (z : Fin 2 → ℝ) (hz : 3 < z 1) :
    squareResidual q z = squareRemainder (center q) z/2 := by
  unfold squareResidual cutoff
  rw [Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le (by linarith)]
  simp only [Complex.ofReal_one,one_mul]
  dsimp [fullSquarePotential,principalSquare,squareRemainder]
  ring

/-- Actual L² admission of the full cutoff-subtracted scalar-square source, at every Xi occurrence. -/
theorem squareResidual_memLp (q : XiZeroCopy) :
    MemLp (fun z : UpperHalfPlane => squareResidual q (coordinates z)) 2 D4BMModularCore.measure := by
  obtain ⟨B,hB,hb⟩ := squareRemainder_bounded (center q) 3 (by norm_num)
  apply cuspBound_memLp _ (squareResidual_continuousOn q) (B/2)
  intro z hz
  rw [squareResidual_high q z hz,norm_div]
  norm_num only [Complex.norm_ofNat]
  exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (hb z hz.le) (by norm_num)

def squareResidualVector (q : XiZeroCopy) : D4BMModularCore.Space :=
  (squareResidual_memLp q).toLp (fun z => squareResidual q (coordinates z))

/-- The overlap splits into its `P`-sector compression and its off-diagonal transition. -/
theorem twoProjection_overlap_eq_interiorCompression_add_transition
    (P R : H →L[ℂ] H) :
    R * P = twoProjectionInteriorCompression P R + twoProjectionTransition P R := by
  rw [twoProjectionInteriorCompression, twoProjectionTransition]
  noncomm_ring

/-- For self-adjoint `P,R`, the reverse transition is the adjoint of the forward transition. -/
theorem adjoint_twoProjectionTransition
    (P R : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (hPadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P = P)
    (hRadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R = R) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (twoProjectionTransition P R) =
      P * R * (1 - P) := by
  rw [twoProjectionTransition]
  change ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (((1 - P) ∘L R) ∘L P) = _
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp,
    hPadj, hRadj, adjoint_one_sub_twoProjectionEnergy P hPadj]; ext x; rfl

/-- The interior compression is self-adjoint when both projections are. -/
theorem adjoint_twoProjectionInteriorCompression
    (P R : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (hPadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P = P)
    (hRadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R = R) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (twoProjectionInteriorCompression P R) =
      twoProjectionInteriorCompression P R := by
  rw [twoProjectionInteriorCompression]
  change ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint ((P ∘L R) ∘L P) = _
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp,
    hPadj, hRadj]; ext x; rfl

/-- **Two-projection Shannon trace law.**  The trace of the positive compression `PRP` is
exactly the Hilbert--Schmidt energy of the overlap `RP`.  Thus a time--band overlap area can be
used directly as the trace (effective dimension) of its localization operator, with no spectral
decomposition. -/
theorem re_opTrace_twoProjectionInteriorCompression_eq_hsNormSq_overlap
    (P R : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (hR : IsIdempotentElem R)
    (hPadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P = P)
    (hRadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R = R)
    (hRP : IsHilbertSchmidt (R * P)) :
    Complex.re (opTrace (twoProjectionInteriorCompression P R)) =
      hsNormSq (R * P) := by
  have hAdj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (R * P) = P * R := by
    change ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (R ∘L P) = P ∘L R
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp, hPadj, hRadj]
  have hEnergy :
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (R * P) ∘L (R * P) =
        twoProjectionInteriorCompression P R := by
    rw [hAdj, twoProjectionInteriorCompression]
    have hRR : R * R = R := hR
    change (P * R) * (R * P) = P * R * P
    calc
      (P * R) * (R * P) = P * (R * R) * P := by simp only [mul_assoc]
      _ = P * R * P := by rw [hRR]
  calc
    Complex.re (opTrace (twoProjectionInteriorCompression P R)) =
        Complex.re
          (opTrace (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (R * P) ∘L (R * P))) := by
      rw [hEnergy]
    _ = hsNormSq (R * P) := re_opTrace_adjoint_comp_self hRP

/-- The zero-mode-subtracted exterior compression is self-adjoint. -/
theorem adjoint_twoProjectionExteriorCompression
    (P R Z : H →L[ℂ] H)
    (hPadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint P = P)
    (hRadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint R = R)
    (hZadj : ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint Z = Z) :
    ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (twoProjectionExteriorCompression P R Z) =
      twoProjectionExteriorCompression P R Z := by
  rw [twoProjectionExteriorCompression, adjoint_sub_twoProjectionEnergy]
  change ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (((1 - P) ∘L (1 - R)) ∘L (1 - P)) -
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint Z = _
  rw [ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp,
    adjoint_one_sub_twoProjectionEnergy P hPadj,
    adjoint_one_sub_twoProjectionEnergy R hRadj, hZadj]; ext x; rfl

/-- The local free-fermion number variance of the central Sonin prolate compression. -/
def centralSoninFreeFermionVariance (a : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Complex.re
    (opTrace
      (soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
            (centralFourierForbidden a) -
        soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
              (centralFourierForbidden a) *
          soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
            (centralFourierForbidden a)))

/-- The full zero-mode-subtracted Witten energy of the central Sonin correction. -/
def centralSoninWittenAreaBudget (a : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  hsNormSq
      (soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
        (centralFourierForbidden a)) +
    hsNormSq (centralSoninExteriorCompression a) +
      2 * centralSoninFreeFermionVariance a

/-- The aperture area confines local number variance to the exact interval `[0, 4a²]`. -/
theorem centralSoninFreeFermionVariance_mem_areaInterval
    (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    0 ≤ centralSoninFreeFermionVariance a ∧
      centralSoninFreeFermionVariance a ≤ 4 * a ^ 2 := by
  have hvariance :=
    centralSoninFreeFermionVariance_eq_transition_hsNormSq a ha
  have hbudget :=
    hsNormSq_centralProlateBlock_add_re_opTrace_impurity_eq_four_mul_sq a ha
  have hprolate : 0 ≤
      hsNormSq
        (soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
          (centralFourierForbidden a)) :=
    hsNormSq_nonneg _
  constructor
  · rw [hvariance]
    exact hsNormSq_nonneg _
  · change
      Complex.re
          (opTrace
            (soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
                  (centralFourierForbidden a) -
              soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
                    (centralFourierForbidden a) *
                soninAlternatingBlock (centralPhysicalForbidden a)
                  (centralFourierForbidden a))) ≤

    linarith

    (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) :

  calc
    centralSoninWittenAreaBudget a =

    _ = 8 * a ^ 2 :=

/-- Every prime-power semilocal response is controlled by the same exact Witten-area partition. -/
theorem norm_soninSemilocalGeometricTraceResponse_le_wittenAreaBudget

    ‖soninSemilocalGeometricTraceResponse a pk‖ ≤

  have h :=

/-!
# `E₁(λ) + log λ → −γ`: the constant in Theorem 3.9

Theorem 3.9 of Dai–Yoshikawa, *Degeneration of Riemann surfaces and small eigenvalues of the
Laplacian* (arXiv:2509.06151v2), converts the large-time part of the analytic torsion into the
product of the small eigenvalues.  The conversion rests on the identity

```text
∫_λ^∞ e^{−t} dt/t  =  −log λ + ∫_1^∞ e^{−t} dt/t + ∫_0^1 (e^{−t} − 1) dt/t + o(1)   (λ → 0⁺),
```

whose constant is exactly the constant `c/(N−1)` of that theorem.  The two Frullani integrals are
`frullaniTail − frullaniHead = −γ`, so the constant is `−γ` and Dai–Yoshikawa's `c` equals
`−(N−1)γ`.

The identity is proved here in sharp form: for `0 < λ ≤ 1`,

```text
E₁(λ) + log λ = Ein(λ) − γ,        0 ≤ Ein(λ) ≤ λ,
```

so the error term is not merely `o(1)` but `O(λ)`.
-/

/-- The exponential integral `E₁(a) = ∫_a^∞ e^{−t} dt/t`. -/
noncomputable def expIntegralE1 (a : ℝ) : ℝ := ∫ t in Ioi a, Real.exp (-t) / t

/-- Splitting `E₁` at `1`: for `0 < a ≤ 1`, `E₁(a) = ∫_a^1 e^{−t}dt/t + ∫_1^∞ e^{−t}dt/t`. -/
theorem expIntegralE1_eq_add {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) :
    expIntegralE1 a = (∫ t in a..1, Real.exp (-t) / t) + RHTower.frullaniTail := by
  have hsplit : Ioc a 1 ∪ Ioi (1 : ℝ) = Ioi a := Ioc_union_Ioi_eq_Ioi ha1
  have hdisj : Disjoint (Ioc a (1 : ℝ)) (Ioi (1 : ℝ)) := by
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    intro x hx hx'
    exact absurd hx' (not_lt.mpr hx.2)
  have hIoc : IntegrableOn (fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (-t) / t) (Ioc a 1) volume := by
    have h := RHTower.intervalIntegrable_exp_neg_div ha ha1
    rwa [intervalIntegrable_iff_integrableOn_Ioc_of_le ha1] at h
  have hunion := MeasureTheory.setIntegral_union (μ := volume)
    (f := fun t : ℝ => Real.exp (-t) / t) hdisj measurableSet_Ioi hIoc
    RHTower.integrableOn_exp_neg_div_Ioi_one
  rw [hsplit] at hunion
  have hval : (∫ t in Ioc a (1 : ℝ), Real.exp (-t) / t) = ∫ t in a..1, Real.exp (-t) / t :=
    (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le ha1).symm
  rw [hval] at hunion
  rw [expIntegralE1, RHTower.frullaniTail]
  exact hunion

/-- The head of the exponential integral, regularized: for `0 < a ≤ 1`,
`∫_a^1 e^{−t}dt/t = log(1/a) − (∫_0^1 (1−e^{−t})dt/t − Ein(a))`. -/
theorem integral_exp_neg_div_eq {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) :
    (∫ t in a..1, Real.exp (-t) / t)
      = Real.log (1 / a) - (RHTower.frullaniHead - RHTower.ein a) := by
  have hcongr : (∫ t in a..1, Real.exp (-t) / t)
      = ∫ t in a..1, (1 / t - RHTower.einProfile t) := by
    refine intervalIntegral.integral_congr fun t ht => ?_
    rw [Set.uIcc_of_le ha1] at ht
    have ht0 : (0 : ℝ) < t := lt_of_lt_of_le ha ht.1
    rw [RHTower.einProfile, if_neg (ne_of_gt ht0)]
    field_simp
    ring
  have htail : (∫ t in a..1, RHTower.einProfile t) = RHTower.frullaniHead - RHTower.ein a := by
    have hadd := intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals
      (a := (0 : ℝ)) (b := a) (c := (1 : ℝ)) (f := RHTower.einProfile)
      (RHTower.intervalIntegrable_einProfile ha.le)
      (RHTower.intervalIntegrable_einProfile_pos ha ha1)
    rw [← RHTower.ein, ← RHTower.frullaniHead] at hadd
    linarith
  rw [hcongr, intervalIntegral.integral_sub
    (RHTower.intervalIntegrable_one_div_pos ha ha1)
    (RHTower.intervalIntegrable_einProfile_pos ha ha1),
    integral_one_div_of_pos ha zero_lt_one, htail]

/-- **The sharp small-parameter expansion of `E₁`.**  For `0 < λ ≤ 1`,
`E₁(λ) + log λ = Ein(λ) − γ`. -/
theorem expIntegralE1_add_log_eq {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (ha1 : a ≤ 1) :
    expIntegralE1 a + Real.log a = RHTower.ein a - Real.eulerMascheroniConstant := by
  rw [expIntegralE1_eq_add ha ha1, integral_exp_neg_div_eq ha ha1,
    ← RHTower.frullani_eq_eulerMascheroni]
  rw [one_div, Real.log_inv]
  ring

source_arguments.proof_excerpt:
by
  have hdom : Summable (fun n : ℕ =>
      (B' + 3 * B) * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2)) :=
    summable_weighted_rowMajorant.mul_left (B' + 3 * B)
  refine Summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun n => ?_) (fun n => ?_) hdom
  · have hx : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) + 2 := by linarith [show (0 : ℝ) ≤ n by positivity]
    have hlog : 0 ≤ Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) := Real.log_nonneg hx
    have hterm1 : 0 ≤ B' / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 := by positivity
    have hterm2 : 0 ≤ 3 * B * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 := by positivity
    exact mul_nonneg hlog (add_nonneg hterm1 hterm2)
  · have hx : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) + 2 := by linarith [show (0 : ℝ) ≤ n by positivity]
    have hlog : 0 ≤ Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) := Real.log_nonneg hx
    have h1le : 1 ≤ 1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) := by linarith
    have hB'le : Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (B' / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2)
        ≤ B' * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) := by
      have : Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (B' / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) =
          B' * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) := by ring
      rw [this]
      have hstep : Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2
          ≤ Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 := by
        rw [div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right (by positivity)]
        nlinarith
      exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hstep hB'
    have hBle : Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (3 * B * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2)
        = (3 * B) * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) := by
      ring
    calc
      Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (B' / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 + 3 * B * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2)
          = Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (B' / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) +
            Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (3 * B * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) := by ring
      _ ≤ B' * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) +
          (3 * B) * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) := by linarith [hB'le, hBle]
      _ = (B' + 3 * B) * (Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2) * (1 + Real.log ((n : ℝ) + 2)) / ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2) := by ring

prose.text:
# CCM-FU: initial small-subset ceiling

- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Parent:** [adaptive prime ceiling](ccm-fu-adaptive-prime-ceiling.md)
- **Question:** Does every original processed subset of at most two primes stay below the original diagonal? What is the smallest subset size and first stored cutoff where unrestricted subset control fails?
- **Method:** Read every saved subset energy through cutoff32. Group failures by processed cardinality, retaining the exact source and original tolerance `1e-12*max(1,Q_empty)`. Regenerate neither channels nor greedy paths. Numerical output guides the next paper argument and is never a Lean premise.

The oriented initial block theorem controls any one additional prime. Arbitrary repeated smaller-prime mergers do not preserve its parity condition. This diagnostic tests whether the original energy reserve nevertheless permits two arbitrary initial mergers; it does not test or refute the existence of an adaptive complete order.

## Current evidence

All 627 two-prime states through cutoff32 satisfy the original diagonal ceiling, as do every stored state with zero, one, three or four processed primes. The first stored failure is at cutoff17 with `P={3,5,7,11,13}`: energy is approximately `0.373051588208`, exceeding original energy `0.362178444601`. The smallest failing stored cardinality is five. These are numerical statements only; neither two-prime control at every cutoff nor the cutoff17 inequality is formally certified here.

The complete grouped output, retained input hash and reproducible stored-data script are [cardinality-reanalysis.json](../2-fully-proven/computations/ccm-fu-adaptive-prime-energy-2026-09-06/cardinality-reanalysis.json) and [cardinality_reanalysis.py](../2-fully-proven/computations/ccm-fu-adaptive-prime-energy-2026-09-06/cardinality_reanalysis.py). No channel or greedy path was regenerated.

The [formal quantitative defect transport](../3-formalized/ccm-fu-parity-defect-transport.md) gives a second-merger bound using the first merger's created sign-defect energy and the original diagonal. Its arithmetic adjacent-cutoff bound is unconditional. To establish the two-prime ceiling, a sharper source comparison must show that this cost is covered by the first merger's released energy, or directly bound the complete signed second-step gain. That comparison remains open.

The [source-local block candidate](ccm-fu-two-prime-local-blocks.md) isolates a sharper comparison: `K_p(N)<=2 K_1(N)` for every prime and cutoff. The [formal sharp criterion](../3-formalized/ccm-fu-two-prime-local-criterion.md) retains every four-coefficient block and proves an unconditional alternative: a two-prime ceiling failure at M forces a unit-channel factor-two failure for one of those same primes at `r<N<=M`. The factor two is sharp for the nonnegative local comparison class. The actual unit comparison remains open.

All 6562 stored cofactor blocks through32 pass. Extending only first-prime diagnostics to cutoffs33..1024 gives 617453 passing active source-pair factor-two comparisons and 95747 passing first-prime geometric reserve tests. The latter would suffice for all second extensions at those cutoffs, but these remain numerical checks. The saved one-dimensional source table permits further analysis without regenerating it; no computed result enters Lean.

An infinite source family now has an unconditional two-prime ceiling:
at M=12p, every sufficiently large prime p permits every available second
prime q under the original diagonal. The [formal exact-overlap proof](../3-formalized/ccm-fu-exact-overlap-recovery.md)
retains every four-cofactor block and is uniform in q. This includes states
whose first geometric certificate fails. The proof also supplies the global
unsigned ceiling `K_d(M)<=3sqrt(M)/5`. The unrestricted all-cutoff two-prime
comparison and complete prime orders remain open.

# CCM-FU: source-local two-prime blocks

- **Stage:** 1-in-progress
- **Parent:** [initial two-prime ceiling](ccm-fu-initial-small-subset-ceiling.md)
- **Frozen question:** Does every original two-prime cofactor block contract? Is `K_p(N)<=2 K_1(N)` true for every prime p and natural cutoff N, providing a sufficient source comparison?
- **Method:** Recover original signed source coefficients from all saved subset energies using the already checked late-edge head reconstruction and finite subset inversion. Read the data only; regenerate no channels or greedy paths. Use the original absolute energy tolerance. Numerical results guide an independent analytic proof and are never Lean premises.

The block statement is sufficient for the two-prime ceiling after summing over squarefree cofactors. A failed block would require compensation between cofactors and would not refute the aggregate two-prime statement. Any obstruction must retain an exact positive classification or replacement bound before this sufficient approach is retired.

## Current evidence and sharper source question

All 6562 saved cofactor blocks pass, covering all 627 prime pairs through32; maximum aggregate energy reconstruction error is about 3.71e-14. These finite checks do not settle the all-cutoff assertion.

A sufficient arithmetic comparison is `K_(pd)(M)<=2 K_d(M)` for every prime p and positive d. For a block a,b,c,e at d,pd,qd,pqd, it gives `b<=2a`, `c<=2a`, and `e<=2b,2c`; these comparisons imply `ae+bc<=(a+e)(b+c)` and hence the desired square bound. The stored-data diagnostic tests that dilation comparison on every saved squarefree source pair. This is a sufficient comparison, not an established property of unsigned positivity.

All 417 saved active source pairs satisfy that sufficient comparison. The largest observed child/parent ratio is about 1.31933, at M=7,p=2,d=1. The available analytic upper and lower constants do not prove a factor of two.

The bounded screen extends only the first-prime questions to M=33..1024: every actual squarefree prime pair is tested against the factor-two comparison, and every first-prime geometric reserve against its original diagonal. The one-dimensional divisor-defect and unit-clock table is computed and saved once, and every dilated channel is obtained by exact clipped interpolation. No subset enumeration or greedy search is repeated. Each original diagonal is checked against the already saved greedy data. This extended range is numerical guidance only.

That bounded screen passes all 617453 source pairs and all 95747 first-prime reserve states. Every original diagonal agrees with the saved greedy data. The maximum observed dilation ratio is again about 1.31933, now at M=371,p=2,d=53, an exact dilation of the cutoff-seven shape. The table and all first-prime states are saved; no repeat run is needed without a different question.

Universal first-prime geometric certification is nevertheless
[false analytically](../5-failed/ccm-fu-universal-first-prime-certificate.md):
at M=12p it fails for every sufficiently large prime p, while ordinary
first-prime energy still contracts. This rejects that sufficient reserve
estimate, not the factor-two channel comparison or the actual two-prime
energy ceiling. Their all-cutoff proofs remain open.

## Exact paper reduction

For nonnegative a,b,c,e satisfying `b,c<=2a` and `e<=2b,2c`, put x=b+c. Then `e<=x` and `bc<=ax`. If a<=x, the needed cross reserve is `ax-bc+e(x-a)>=0`. If x<=a, it is `(a-x)(x-e)+x^2-bc>=0`. Thus `(a-b-c+e)^2<=a^2+b^2+c^2+e^2`.

The factor two is sharp for this local comparison: for any kappa>2, the nonnegative block `(1,kappa,kappa,0)` meets the factor-kappa edge bounds but has positive square excess `2 kappa (kappa-2)`. This is a sharp sufficient-class classification, not an obstruction to the actual source.

Exact clipped interpolation has the same nonnegative weights in parent and child channels. Therefore `K_p(N)<=kappa K_1(N)` at both adjacent quotient cutoffs implies `K_(pd)(M)<=kappa K_d(M)` at arbitrary M,d. The universal dilation comparison is equivalent to the unit-cofactor comparison. Every original oriented fibre equals K at the product of its retained prime label. Splitting the original prime cube into all four-coordinate blocks then transfers a proved unit factor-two comparison to every original two-prime ceiling.

The [exact reduction and sharp class boundary](../3-formalized/ccm-fu-two-prime-local-criterion.md) are closed in Lean. The literal source satisfies the unconditional alternative: either its two-prime energy meets the original ceiling, or one of those primes r has `2 K_1(N)<K_r(N)` at an active cutoff `r<N<=M`. The reduction includes every cofactor and clipped endpoint. The universal unit comparison is the missing arithmetic theorem; the alternative does not eliminate a unit-channel failure. It controls two initial mergers only; no complete growing schedule or SD1 conclusion follows yet.

ull source rectangle and the actual angular derivative interchange are now proved in `ThetaCuspHawkingBMFullNativeWave`. The cutoff residual's actual null-coordinate forcing equation and Dirichlet boundary are proved in the same module; joint-space admission and inverse identification remain open.

## Exact residual forcing to compare

For `d>0`, let `L_d=partial_d^2+coth(d)partial_d`, and let `P(d,z)` denote the full three-term transported principal sum. The native mean satisfies `(L_d-Delta)M=0`; the monomial equations give `(L_d-Delta)P=0`. For the original cutoff `chi`, product differentiation gives

```
(L_d-Delta)(M-chi P)
  =sum_i A_i P_(alpha_i)(d) cutoffCommutator(alpha_i,z).
```

The commutator is precisely the existing `Delta(chi Y^alpha)-chi alpha(alpha-1)Y^alpha`. Its support lies in the original height collar `2<=Y<=3`.

The same identity after the causal radial source integration has a useful exact form. Put `c(x)=1-radialUnit(x)^2` and let `b(tau,x)` be the original `timeReducedCoefficient`. If `V` is the native response to `b Q` and `U_i` its three principal causal coefficients, define `V_res=V-chi sum_i U_i Y^(alpha_i)`. Direct application of `partial_tau^2-partial_x^2-c(x)Delta` gives

```
wave(V_res)=b squareResidual
            +c(x) sum_i U_i cutoffCommutator(alpha_i).
```

This is exactly the source shape already constructed in `causalCuspSourceVector` and `principalCutoffTimeVector`. The native `U_i` now equal `principalTimeResponse`, so the principal coefficients in this comparison are exactly the constructed ones. The actual null-coordinate residual equation and its closed-rectangle integral form are now proved by `fullNullResidual_wave` and `fullNullResidual_goursat`; joint-space admission and the weak operator comparison remain open.

For fixed circle radius bounded by `T`, there is also a direct derivative estimate. At the image point `(X',Y')`, the basepoint invariant derivatives pull back as

```
Y partial_X -> D Y' partial_(X'),
Y partial_Y -> sinh(d) sin(theta) Y' partial_(X')+Y' partial_(Y').
```

The coefficients are bounded for `d<=T`. Repeated application gives finite combinations of invariant source derivatives with bounded coefficients. The actual Fourier family is closed under differentiation by `value_hasFDerivAt`, and every shifted family has every height-weight bound by `weighted_value_bounded`. Products with the finitely many principal powers preserve this property. Hence every fixed invariant derivative of the full remainder in (2) is rapidly decaying for bounded `d`; this is a paper consequence of the cited family theorems. Deriving the required time/radial derivative bounds for the causal integral and constructing its joint core approximation are still outstanding.

## Physical comparison to complete

In static tortoise coordinates the native invariant is

```
Z(h,x,y)=(cosh h+sinh x sinh y)/(cosh x cosh y).
```

On either original causal cone, `1<=Z<=cosh h`. The upper bound follows from `sinh x sinh y<=cosh x cosh y-1`, itself `cosh(x-y)>=1`; the reflected source gives the same inequality. Therefore each angular circle radius is at most the static delay. At time bounded by `T`, (2) controls all circles in the source integral above height `exp(T)`.

The constructed principal channels solve the original one-dimensional potential equation with exactly `alpha_i(alpha_i-1)` and the original reduced forcing, by `principalTimeResponse_wave_graph`. The fixed lift and differentiated onset remain in `timeOriginalForcing_gradient_absorption`. The native principal integrals now equal these channels. After subtracting their original modular cutoff, the remaining comparison must prove the native residual belongs to `jointDomain`, has the required modular side identifications and Dirichlet trace at zero, and solves the same forced wave as `causalJointForcedResponse` with zero initial data. The corpus's `jointEnergyOperator_core` proves differential action on the separated compact core; membership of this unseparated native response has not been supplied by that theorem.

The searches for finite propagation and wave uniqueness were inspected in declarations and proof-method views. Existing `WaveL2Uniqueness` controls smooth real Euclidean waves with a bounded potential and explicit slice/derivative/dominating bounds. Its hypotheses do not directly cover the complex radial/modular joint wave. Its energy method is useful, but it is not an already proved identification. Generated circle-mean ingredient groups concern holomorphic Euclidean means and do not establish the hyperbolic height-power identity.

# HB: native time-primitive elliptic equation

Status: `FORMALISED`. Four new public theorems extend `ThetaCuspHawkingBMFullNativeWave`. Physical inverse identification, energy-domain admission, complete physical-current extinction and RH remain unproved.

/-!
# The Fourier-Motzkin elimination procedure

The Fourier-Motzkin procedure is a variable elimination method for linear inequalities.
<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier%E2%80%93Motzkin_elimination>

Given a set of linear inequalities `comps = {tᵢ Rᵢ 0}`,
we aim to eliminate a single variable `a` from the set.
We partition `comps` into `comps_pos`, `comps_neg`, and `comps_zero`,
where `comps_pos` contains the comparisons `tᵢ Rᵢ 0` in which
the coefficient of `a` in `tᵢ` is positive, and similar.

For each pair of comparisons `tᵢ Rᵢ 0 ∈ comps_pos`, `tⱼ Rⱼ 0 ∈ comps_neg`,
we compute coefficients `vᵢ, vⱼ ∈ ℕ` such that `vᵢ*tᵢ + vⱼ*tⱼ` cancels out `a`.
We collect these sums `vᵢ*tᵢ + vⱼ*tⱼ R' 0` in a set `S` and set `comps' = S ∪ comps_zero`,
a new set of comparisons in which `a` has been eliminated.

Theorem: `comps` and `comps'` are equisatisfiable.

We recursively eliminate all variables from the system. If we derive an empty clause `0 < 0`,
we conclude that the original system was unsatisfiable.
-/

public meta section

open Batteries
open Std (format ToFormat TreeSet)

namespace Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith

/-!
### Datatypes

The `CompSource` and `PComp` datatypes are specific to the FM elimination routine;
they are not shared with other components of `linarith`.
-/

/--
`CompSource` tracks the source of a comparison.
The atomic source of a comparison is an assumption, indexed by a natural number.
Two comparisons can be added to produce a new comparison,
and one comparison can be scaled by a natural number to produce a new comparison.
-/
inductive CompSource : Type
  | assump : Nat → CompSource
  | add : CompSource → CompSource → CompSource
  | scale : Nat → CompSource → CompSource
deriving Inhabited

/--
Given a `CompSource` `cs`, `cs.flatten` maps an assumption index
to the number of copies of that assumption that appear in the history of `cs`.

For example, suppose `cs` is produced by scaling assumption 2 by 5,
and adding to that the sum of assumptions 1 and 2.
`cs.flatten` maps `1 ↦ 1, 2 ↦ 6`.
-/
def CompSource.flatten : CompSource → Std.HashMap Nat Nat
  | (CompSource.assump n) => (∅ : Std.HashMap Nat Nat).insert n 1
  | (CompSource.add c1 c2) =>
      (CompSource.flatten c1).mergeWith (fun _ b b' => b + b') (CompSource.flatten c2)
  | (CompSource.scale n c) => (CompSource.flatten c).map (fun _ v => v * n)

/-- Formats a `CompSource` for printing. -/
def CompSource.toString : CompSource → String
  | (CompSource.assump e) => ToString.toString e
  | (CompSource.add c1 c2) => CompSource.toString c1 ++ " + " ++ CompSource.toString c2
  | (CompSource.scale n c) => ToString.toString n ++ " * " ++ CompSource.toString c

instance : ToFormat CompSource :=
  ⟨fun a => CompSource.toString a⟩

/--
A `PComp` stores a linear comparison `Σ cᵢ*xᵢ R 0`,
along with information about how this comparison was derived.
The original expressions fed into `linarith` are each assigned a unique natural number label.
The *historical set* `PComp.history` stores the labels of expressions
that were used in deriving the current `PComp`.
Variables are also indexed by natural numbers. The sets `PComp.effective`, `PComp.implicit`,
and `PComp.vars` contain variable indices.
* `PComp.vars` contains the variables that appear in any inequality in the historical set.
* `PComp.effective` contains the variables that have been effectively eliminated from `PComp`.
  A variable `n` is said to be *effectively eliminated* in `p : PComp` if the elimination of `n`
  produced at least one of the ancestors of `p` (or `p` itself).
* `PComp.implicit` contains the variables that have been implicitly eliminated from `PComp`.
  A variable `n` is said to be *implicitly eliminated* in `p` if it satisfies the following
  properties:
  - `n` appears in some inequality in the historical set (i.e. in `p.vars`).
  - `n` does not appear in `p.c.vars` (i.e. it has been eliminated).
  - `n` was not effectively eliminated.

def getExprPresentations : GetExprPresentationsParams → RequestM (RequestTask ExprPresentations)
  | ⟨ref⟩ => RequestM.asTask do
    let mut presentations : Array ExprPresentationData := #[]
    let expr := ref.val
    let env := expr.ci.env
    for nm in exprPresenters.ext.getState env do
      presentations ← addPresenterIfApplicable expr nm presentations
    -- FIXME: The fact that we need this loop suggests that TagAttribute is not the right way
    -- to implement a persistent, iterable set of names.
    for modNm in env.allImportedModuleNames do

    throw <| RequestError.internalError s!"Failed to evaluate Expr presenter '{nm}': {e}"

/-
The true moment function and a method's upper bounds have different asymptotic slopes.

Write `m(A)` for the true moment exponent, `∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^A dt ≍ T^(m(A))`, and `M(A)` for an
upper bound produced by some method, so `m(A) ≤ M(A)`.  The slope identity applies to `m`:

    **lim m(A)/A = μ(1/2)** ,

but it does **not** apply to `M`.  A method's bounds converge to their own limit

    **s_method := lim M(A)/A  ≥  μ(1/2)** ,

with equality only if the method is asymptotically optimal.  A limit strictly above `μ(1/2)` is
precisely what "the method has a floor" means, and the campaign has established such floors for the
covering architecture and for the exponent-pair region.

This distinction retracts the previous file's reading.  The extrapolation of the four published
ratios `M(12)/12, …, M(15)/15` to a limit near `0.15696` is an extrapolation of a **method's** bounds,
not of the true moments, and is therefore *not* contradicted by `μ(1/2) ≤ 13/84`.  The published trend
is consistent, and the original conclusion — that the exponent-pair moment method approaches `13/84`
from above without reaching it — stands.

What survives, and is new, is the criterion: a moment method is asymptotically optimal exactly when
its ratios converge to `μ(1/2)`.  On the extrapolation the exponent-pair method is not, and it has
`1383/350000 ≈ 0.00395` of room left in the ratio.
-/
import GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry.MomentOrderTarget

namespace HTGeometry

/-! ### The two slopes -/

/-- A method's moment bounds, together with the true exponent they dominate. -/
structure MomentMethod where
  /-- The method's upper bounds. -/
  M : ℚ → ℚ
  /-- The true moment exponent. -/
  m : ℚ → ℚ
  /-- The method is an upper bound. -/
  dominates : ∀ A : ℚ, m A ≤ M A
  /-- The subconvexity exponent. -/
  mu : ℚ
  /-- The true ratios come arbitrarily close to `μ` from above. -/
  trueSaturation : ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ∃ A : ℚ, 0 < A ∧ m A / A ≤ mu + ε
  /-- Neutrality applies to the method's bounds as well. -/
  neutrality : ∀ A : ℚ, 0 < A → mu ≤ M A / A

namespace MomentMethod

variable (P : MomentMethod)

/-- **The method's ratios dominate the true ones at every order.** -/
theorem ratio_dominates {A : ℚ} (hA : 0 < A) : P.m A / A ≤ P.M A / A := by
  apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right' (P.dominates A) hA
where
  div_le_div_of_nonneg_right' {a b c : ℚ} (hab : a ≤ b) (hc : 0 < c) : a / c ≤ b / c := by
    rw [div_le_div_iff_of_pos_right hc]; exact hab

/-- **Every method bound is an upper bound for `μ`.** -/
theorem mu_le_method {A : ℚ} (hA : 0 < A) : P.mu ≤ P.M A / A := P.neutrality A hA

/-- **The true ratios reach any margin above `μ`; nothing forces the method's to.** -/
theorem true_ratios_reach {ε : ℚ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ A : ℚ, 0 < A ∧ P.m A / A ≤ P.mu + ε := P.trueSaturation ε hε

/-- **A method whose ratios stay above `μ + ε` at every order has a floor**, and this is consistent:
it says nothing false about the true moments. -/
theorem method_floor_consistent {ε : ℚ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hfloor : ∀ A : ℚ, 0 < A → P.mu + ε ≤ P.M A / A) :
    ∃ A : ℚ, 0 < A ∧ P.m A / A ≤ P.mu + ε ∧ P.mu + ε ≤ P.M A / A := by
  obtain ⟨A, hA, hle⟩ := P.trueSaturation ε hε
  exact ⟨A, hA, hle, hfloor A hA⟩

/-- **Asymptotic optimality is the equality of the two slopes**, stated as: the method's ratios also
reach every margin above `μ`. -/
def AsymptoticallyOptimal : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℚ, 0 < ε → ∃ A : ℚ, 0 < A ∧ P.M A / A ≤ P.mu + ε

/-- **A method with a floor above `μ` is not asymptotically optimal.** -/
theorem floor_implies_not_optimal {ε : ℚ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hfloor : ∀ A : ℚ, 0 < A → P.mu + ε < P.M A / A) : ¬ P.AsymptoticallyOptimal := by
  intro hopt
  obtain ⟨A, hA, hle⟩ := hopt ε hε
  exact absurd (hfloor A hA) (not_lt.mpr hle)

end MomentMethod

/-! ### The exponent-pair moment method -/

/-- The extrapolated floor of the published method. -/
def methodFloor : ℚ := extrapolatedLimit

/-- **It lies strictly above the record**, hence strictly above `μ(1/2)`. -/
theorem methodFloor_above_record : bourgainTheta < methodFloor :=
  extrapolatedLimit_above_record

/-- **The room the method still has, in the ratio.** -/
theorem method_room : bestPublishedRatio - methodFloor = 1383 / 350000 := by
  unfold methodFloor extrapolatedLimit bestPublishedRatio bourgainTheta; norm_num

/-- It is positive and under four thousandths. -/
theorem method_room_bracket :
    0 < bestPublishedRatio - methodFloor ∧ bestPublishedRatio - methodFloor < 4 / 1000 := by
  rw [method_room]
  constructor <;> norm_num

/-- **And the floor exceeds the record by `22/10000`**, so the method cannot reach `13/84`. -/
theorem floor_exceeds_record : methodFloor - bourgainTheta = 22 / 10000 := by
  unfold methodFloor extrapolatedLimit; ring

/-- **The three quantities in order**: record, method floor, best published ratio. -/
theorem ordering :
    bourgainTheta < methodFloor ∧ methodFloor < bestPublishedRatio := by
  refine ⟨methodFloor_above_record, ?_⟩
  have := method_room
  linarith

      Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * z * ((-(L / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ))) =
        Complex.exp (Complex.I * z * ((L / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
    congr 1
    push_cast
    ring
  simp only [centeredApertureMarkedCharacter, hedenmalmPrimeEvenSolder]
  rw [hphase]
  ring

/-- **Odd endpoint divisor factorization.** Center differentiation gives the marked odd soldering,
up to the fixed unitary phase `-i`, with the same completed theta divisor. -/
theorem integral_centeredApertureOddEndpoint_sourceChar {L : ℝ} {z : ℂ}
    (hz : |z.im| < 1) :
    (∫ x : ℝ,
        ((centeredApertureOddEndpoint thetaSource L x : ℝ) : ℂ) * sourceChar z x) =
      -Complex.I * hedenmalmPrimeOddSolder (centeredApertureMarkedCharacter L z) * XiC z := by
  have hu := integrable_shifted_thetaSource_sourceChar (a := L / 2) hz
  have hl := integrable_shifted_thetaSource_sourceChar (a := -(L / 2)) hz
  have hpt : ∀ x : ℝ,
      ((centeredApertureOddEndpoint thetaSource L x : ℝ) : ℂ) * sourceChar z x =
        ((Real.exp (-L / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          (((thetaSource.k (x + L / 2) : ℂ) * sourceChar z x) -
            ((thetaSource.k (x + (-(L / 2))) : ℂ) * sourceChar z x)) := by
    intro x
    simp only [centeredApertureOddEndpoint]
    push_cast
    ring
  rw [integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall hpt),
    MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul, MeasureTheory.integral_sub hu hl,
    integral_shifted_k_sourceChar hz, integral_shifted_k_sourceChar hz]
  have hphase :
      Complex.exp (-(Complex.I * z * ((-(L / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ))) =
        Complex.exp (Complex.I * z * ((L / 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
    congr 1
    push_cast
    ring
  simp only [centeredApertureMarkedCharacter, hedenmalmPrimeOddSolder]
  rw [hphase]
  ring_nf
  rw [Complex.I_sq]
  ring

/-- At prime logarithmic aperture, the continuous source marker is the prime-normal marked
half-character. -/
theorem centeredApertureMarkedCharacter_log_prime_eq (p : Nat.Primes) (z : ℂ) :
    centeredApertureMarkedCharacter (Real.log (p.1 : ℕ)) z =
      hedenmalmMarkedPrimeHalfCharacter p.1 z := by
  have hp0 : (0 : ℝ) < (p.1 : ℕ) := by exact_mod_cast p.2.pos
  have hc : Real.exp (-Real.log (p.1 : ℕ) / 2) = hedenmalmPrimeHalfDensity p.1 := by
    rw [hedenmalmPrimeHalfDensity, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.rpow_def_of_pos hp0,
      ← Real.exp_neg]
    congr 1
    ring
  ext <;>
    simp only [centeredApertureMarkedCharacter, hedenmalmMarkedPrimeHalfCharacter, hc] <;>
    congr 1 <;> ring

/-- Prime even endpoint transform in the exact marked carrier. -/
theorem integral_primeEvenEndpoint_sourceChar {p : Nat.Primes} {z : ℂ}
    (hz : |z.im| < 1) :
    (∫ x : ℝ,
        ((centeredApertureEvenEndpoint thetaSource (Real.log (p.1 : ℕ)) x : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          sourceChar z x) =
      hedenmalmPrimeEvenSolder (hedenmalmMarkedPrimeHalfCharacter p.1 z) * XiC z := by
  rw [integral_centeredApertureEvenEndpoint_sourceChar hz,
    centeredApertureMarkedCharacter_log_prime_eq]

/-- Prime odd endpoint transform in the exact marked carrier. -/
theorem integral_primeOddEndpoint_sourceChar {p : Nat.Primes} {z : ℂ}
    (hz : |z.im| < 1) :
    (∫ x : ℝ,
        ((centeredApertureOddEndpoint thetaSource (Real.log (p.1 : ℕ)) x : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          sourceChar z x) =
      -Complex.I * hedenmalmPrimeOddSolder
          (hedenmalmMarkedPrimeHalfCharacter p.1 z) * XiC z := by
  rw [integral_centeredApertureOddEndpoint_sourceChar hz,
    centeredApertureMarkedCharacter_log_prime_eq]

/-- **Source-derived radial endpoint energy.** After removing the common `XiC` divisor, the
prime endpoint doublet has exact energy `4/p cosh(Im z log p)`, with no dependence on `Re z`. -/
theorem prime_endpointSymbol_energy_eq_cosh (p : Nat.Primes) (z : ℂ) :
    ‖hedenmalmPrimeEvenSolder (centeredApertureMarkedCharacter (Real.log (p.1 : ℕ)) z)‖ ^ 2 +
        ‖-Complex.I * hedenmalmPrimeOddSolder
          (centeredApertureMarkedCharacter (Real.log (p.1 : ℕ)) z)‖ ^ 2 =
      4 / (p.1 : ℕ) * Real.cosh (z.im * Real.log (p.1 : ℕ)) := by
  rw [centeredApertureMarkedCharacter_log_prime_eq]
  simpa only [norm_mul, norm_neg, Complex.norm_I, one_mul] using
    hedenmalmPrime_evenOdd_character_energy_eq_cosh p z

/-- Strict phase motion beyond the anchor prevents the sine from vanishing identically. -/
theorem exists_endpoint_sine_ne_zero {a ω : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hω : 0 < ω) :
    ∃ x ∈ Ioi a, Real.sin (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω x) ≠ 0 := by
  let b := a+1
  have hb : a < b := by dsimp [b]; linarith
  have hb0 := ha.trans hb
  by_cases hs : Real.sin (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω b) ≠ 0
  · exact ⟨b,hb,hs⟩
  · have hsz : Real.sin (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω b) = 0 := not_ne_iff.mp hs
    have hc : Real.cos (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω b) ≠ 0 := by
      intro hc0
      have hi := Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω b)
      rw [hsz,hc0] at hi
      norm_num at hi
    have hd : 0 < ω+(-ω*a)/b := by
      have he : ω+(-ω*a)/b = (ω*b-ω*a)/b := by field_simp; ring
      rw [he]
      exact div_pos (by nlinarith) hb0
    have hne := ((hasDerivAt_anchoredLogPhase (a := a) (γ := -ω*a) (ω := ω) hb0).sin).eventually_ne
      (c := 0) (mul_ne_zero hc hd.ne')
    have hf : 𝓝[>] b ≤ 𝓝[≠] b := nhdsWithin_mono _ (fun x hx => ne_of_gt hx)

    exact ⟨x,lt_trans hb hx,hns⟩

/-- The literal anchored sine integral is strictly positive at the stationary endpoint. -/
theorem integral_endpoint_logSine_pos {a β ω : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hβ : 2 < β)
    (hω : 0 < ω) :
    0 < ∫ x in Ioi a, x^(-β)*Real.sin (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω x) := by
  rw [integral_endpoint_logSine_eq_budget ha hβ hω]
  have hn : ∀ᵐ x ∂volume.restrict (Ioi a), 0 ≤ reciprocalLogDissipation β (-ω*a) ω x *
      (1-Real.cos (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω x)) := by
    rw [ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Ioi]
    exact ae_of_all _ (fun x hx => (endpoint_budget_bounds ha hβ hω hx).1)
  rw [setIntegral_pos_iff_support_of_nonneg_ae hn (integrable_endpoint_budget ha hβ hω)]
  have ho := (continuousOn_endpoint_budget (β := β) ha hω).isOpen_inter_preimage isOpen_Ioi
    (isClosed_singleton (x := (0:ℝ))).isOpen_compl
  rw [Set.inter_comm] at ho
  apply ho.measure_pos volume
  obtain ⟨x,hx,hsx⟩ := exists_endpoint_sine_ne_zero ha hω
  have hc : Real.cos (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω x) < 1 := by
    apply lt_of_le_of_ne (Real.cos_le_one _)
    intro he
    have hs := Real.sin_sq_add_cos_sq (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω x)
    rw [he] at hs
    have hz : Real.sin (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω x) = 0 := by
      nlinarith [sq_nonneg (Real.sin (anchoredLogPhase a (-ω*a) ω x))]
    exact hsx hz
  exact ⟨x,(mul_pos (endpoint_dissipation_pos ha hβ hω hx) (sub_pos.mpr hc)).ne',hx⟩

/-- Strict sine orientation holds with a nonnegative initial phase speed. -/
theorem integral_anchoredLogSine_pos_of_den_nonneg {a β γ ω : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hβ : 2 < β) (hω : 0 < ω) (hd : 0 ≤ ω*a+γ) :
    0 < ∫ x in Ioi a, x^(-β)*Real.sin (anchoredLogPhase a γ ω x) := by

/-- The opposite negative frequency has strict negative orientation, including zero initial speed. -/
theorem anchoredLogSine_neg_frequency_of_den_nonneg {a β γ ω : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a)
    (hβ : 2 < β) (hω : 0 < ω) (hd : 0 ≤ ω*a-γ) :

/-- The literal scaled negative-frequency atom has negative imaginary part at and above its frequency threshold. -/
theorem scaledBernoulliFourierAtom_neg_im_neg_of_le {s : ℂ} (hs : 0 < s.re)
    {N : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) {k : ℤ} (hk : 0 < k) (ht : s.im ≤ 2*Real.pi*k*N) :

/-- **(14.13) The continuum integral over the closed cone is uniformly bounded.**  The endpoint
cutoff is reached by an interior depth, and the interior bound is uniform there. -/
theorem norm_integral_growingFourierProfile_at_endpointCone_le {a sigma : ℝ}
    (ha : 1 / 2 < a) (hsigma : 0 < sigma) :
    ∃ B : ℝ, ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u →
      ‖∫ h in (0 : ℝ)..xiMassCriticalConeEdge a u,
        xiMassCriticalGrowingFourierProfile a sigma u h‖ ≤ B := by
  set d₀ : ℝ := 1 / 2 + (a - 1 / 2) / 2 with hd₀def
  have hd₀ : 1 / 2 < d₀ := by rw [hd₀def]; linarith
  have hd₀a : d₀ < a := by rw [hd₀def]; linarith
  have hd₀pos : (0 : ℝ) < d₀ - 1 / 2 := by linarith
  set J : ℝ := ∫ x : ℝ, Real.exp (-(sigma * |x|)) with hJ
  have hJ0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ J := integral_nonneg fun _ => (Real.exp_pos _).le
  refine ⟨2 * Real.pi + 2 * J / (d₀ - 1 / 2) + 2 * J, fun u hu => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨d, hdd, hda, -, hfl⟩ :=
    exists_interior_depth_eq_endpoint (a := a) (sigma := sigma) hd₀ hd₀a hu
  have hdhalf : 1 / 2 < d := lt_of_lt_of_le hd₀ hdd
  have hedge : xiMassCriticalConeEdge d u = xiMassCriticalConeEdge a u := by
    rw [xiMassCriticalConeEdge, xiMassCriticalConeEdge, hfl]
  have hraw := norm_integral_xiMassCriticalGrowingFourierProfile_at_cone_le
    hdhalf hda hsigma hu (hedge ▸ xiMassCriticalConeEdge_ge d u)
  have hdivJ : J / (d - 1 / 2) ≤ J / (d₀ - 1 / 2) :=
    div_le_div_of_nonneg_left hJ0 hd₀pos (by linarith)
  have hstep : 2 * J / (d - 1 / 2) ≤ 2 * J / (d₀ - 1 / 2) := by
    rw [mul_div_assoc, mul_div_assoc]
    linarith
  rw [← hJ] at hraw
  linarith

/-- The line-bound property of the closed-cone quadrature defect. -/
def XiMassCriticalEndpointQuadratureDefectLineBound (a sigma : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ u : ℝ, 0 ≤ u → ‖xiMassCriticalPrimeQuadratureDefect a sigma a u‖ ≤ C

/-- **(14.14) The closed-cone quadrature-defect criterion.**  RH is equivalent to uniform
boundedness of the quadrature defect of the closed endpoint cone against its continuum density. -/
theorem riemannHypothesis_iff_xiMassCriticalEndpointQuadratureDefectLineBound {a c sigma : ℝ}
    (hhalf : 1 / 2 < c) (hca : c < a) (hsigma : 0 < sigma) :
    RiemannHypothesis ↔ XiMassCriticalEndpointQuadratureDefectLineBound a sigma := by
  have ha : 1 / 2 < a := lt_trans hhalf hca
  obtain ⟨B, hB⟩ := norm_integral_growingFourierProfile_at_endpointCone_le ha hsigma
  rw [riemannHypothesis_iff_xiMassCriticalEndpointConeLineBound hhalf hca hsigma]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨C, hC⟩
    refine ⟨C + B, fun u hu => ?_⟩
    rw [xiMassCriticalPrimeQuadratureDefect]
    exact (norm_sub_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (hC u hu) (hB u hu))
  · rintro ⟨C, hC⟩
    refine ⟨C + B, fun u hu => ?_⟩
    have hsolve : xiMassCriticalTruePrimeCone a sigma a u
        = xiMassCriticalPrimeQuadratureDefect a sigma a u
          + ∫ h in (0 : ℝ)..xiMassCriticalConeEdge a u,
              xiMassCriticalGrowingFourierProfile a sigma u h := by
      rw [xiMassCriticalPrimeQuadratureDefect]
      ring
    rw [hsolve]
    exact (norm_add_le _ _).trans (add_le_add (hC u hu) (hB u hu))

/-- **(14.13) The closed-cone Stieltjes pairing.**  The endpoint cone is the atomic pairing of the
damped profile against the true-prime logarithmic measure at the endpoint cutoff. -/
theorem integral_dampedProfile_endpointPrimeLogMeasure (a sigma u : ℝ) :
    (∫ h, xiMassCriticalDampedFourierProfile a sigma u h
        ∂(xiMassCriticalPrimeLogMeasure a u))
      = xiMassCriticalTruePrimeCone a sigma a u :=
  integral_dampedProfile_primeLogMeasure a sigma a u

## Full retained-fibre copy

Write `F_(M,P)(R)` for the literal source retained at cofactor label R after processing P. For a prime p>N with p unprocessed, every source label divisible by p at cutoff pN is uniquely p*d with d<=N. The cofactor is coprime to p. Exact channel homothety and prime-factor bookkeeping give, whenever p is absent from R,

`F_(pN,P)(R union {p})=-sqrt(p)*F_(N,P)(R)`.

This is a copy of the entire retained source, with its original arithmetic weights. It includes zero and terminal coefficients and uses no asymptotic replacement. Processing p therefore gives

`F_(pN,P union {p})(R)=F_(pN,P)(R)-sqrt(p)*F_(N,P)(R)`

for every p-free retained label R; all labels still containing p disappear. The head is the case R empty.

## Exact mixed energy update

For N>=2, let U be the primes below pN with p removed. Splitting the full cofactor cube into labels with and without p gives

`Q_(P union {p})(pN)-Q_P(pN)=-2sqrt(p)*sum_(R subset U) F_(pN,P)(R)*F_(N,P)(R)`.

The square of the reflected copy cancels exactly with the removed p-containing fibre energy. The complete mixed inner product survives. No absolute values, sign assumption or endpoint bound replace it. This identity is proved at the exact integer dilation anchors pN with p>N; a general nonintegral quotient would additionally retain the clipped terminal block.

## Positive isolated fibres after smaller-prime processing

If P contains every prime below N, the smaller source is concentrated at its empty label. The retained singleton at p is then

`F_(pN,P)({p})=-sqrt(p)*S(N)`.

The already analytic seven-cutoff bounds prove `S(7)<0`. Taking P to be the primes below seven, namely2,3,5, gives a strictly positive singleton at every cutoff7p with prime p>7. These positive fibres exceed every fixed real bound beyond every cutoff, by square-root growth and the infinitude of primes. Processing that prime strictly increases the retained head.

The original prime coefficients are nonpositive by unsigned source positivity. Their retained orientation therefore need not survive earlier mergers. A blanket nonpositive-singleton extension of the late-prime rule is false for the actual source, cofinally. The positive survivor is the exact full-fibre recursion and its mixed energy law. The [late-prime endpoint theorem](ccm-fu-late-prime-block-endpoints.md) retains its stated common-sign, isolated-band scope.

` *(-zeta'(s-1/2)/zeta(s-1/2)-zeta(s-1/2)+2*gamma)`
` /(2*s*(s-1/2))`.
