import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RetainedPrimeLandauSeparation
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
import Mathlib.Topology.Order.Lattice

/-!
# Finite clipping-stable source margins on every retained prime field

Unconditional Landau separation supplies an actual source cutoff for every
nonzero retained direction. Compactness of the finite coordinate unit sphere
extracts finitely many cutoffs with one positive homogeneous margin. Finite
source-mass bounds preserve that margin under independent sufficiently small
adjacent-cutoff clipping. The pairing is exactly the coordinate pairing with
the complete source vector grouped by retained prime-intersection labels.
These witnesses depend on the retained field; cofinal energy propagation is
not asserted.
-/

noncomputable section
open Complex Set Metric
namespace RHTower

/-- All subsets of the finite retained prime field, including the empty label. -/
abbrev retainedPrimeFieldIndex (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) :=
  ↥((Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ))).powerset)

/-- Real coordinates of a functional on the complete finite retained field. -/
abbrev retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) := retainedPrimeFieldIndex Q → ℝ

private def retainedFieldExtension (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (R : Finset ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if h : R ∈ (Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ))).powerset then z ⟨R, h⟩ else 0

/-- Pairing with the complete actual retained field at one source cutoff. -/
def retainedPrimeFieldPairing (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (M : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Finset.Icc 1 M,
    z ⟨d.primeFactors ∩ Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)),
      Finset.mem_powerset.mpr Finset.inter_subset_right⟩ * mobiusDivisorDilationChannel M d

private lemma fieldPairing_eq_sourceMean (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (M : ℕ) :
    retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M =
      (retainedPrimeSourceMean (Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)))
        (fun R => (retainedFieldExtension Q z R : ℂ)) M).re := by
  simp [retainedPrimeFieldPairing, retainedPrimeSourceMean, retainedFieldExtension,
    Finset.mem_powerset.mpr Finset.inter_subset_right]

lemma continuous_retainedPrimeFieldPairing (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) (M : ℕ) :
    Continuous (fun z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q => retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M) := by
  unfold retainedPrimeFieldPairing
  fun_prop

lemma retainedPrimeFieldPairing_smul (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (c : ℝ) (M : ℕ) :
    retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q (c • z) M = c * retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M := by
  simp [retainedPrimeFieldPairing, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]

/-- Every nonzero direction in the complete retained field is strictly detected
by an actual source cutoff. -/
lemma exists_positive_retainedPrimeFieldPairing (Q : Finset Nat.Primes)
    (z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) (hz : z ≠ 0) :
    ∃ M : ℕ, 0 < retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M := by
  have hcoord : ∃ R : retainedPrimeFieldIndex Q, z R ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra hn
    push Not at hn
    apply hz
    funext R
    exact hn R
  obtain ⟨R, hR⟩ := hcoord
  have hy : ∃ S : Finset ℕ, S ⊆ Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)) ∧
      retainedFieldExtension Q z S ≠ 0 := by
    refine ⟨R.1, Finset.mem_powerset.mp R.2, ?_⟩
    simpa only [retainedFieldExtension, dif_pos R.2] using hR
  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := exists_positive_retainedPrimeSourceMean Q (retainedFieldExtension Q z) hy
  exact ⟨M, by rwa [fieldPairing_eq_sourceMean]⟩

/-- Each finite retained field has a finite family of actual source cutoffs and
one uniform positive directional margin. The cutoffs depend on the retained field. -/
theorem exists_retainedPrimeField_finite_uniform_margin (Q : Finset Nat.Primes) :
    ∃ K : Finset ℕ, K.Nonempty ∧ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
      ∀ z : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q, ∃ M ∈ K,
        c * ‖z‖ ≤ retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M := by
  letI : Nonempty (retainedPrimeFieldIndex Q) := ⟨⟨∅, by simp⟩⟩
  let S := sphere (0 : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) 1
  have hS : IsCompact S := isCompact_sphere _ _
  have hSne : S.Nonempty := by
    refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
    simp [S]
  let U : ℕ → Set (retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q) := fun M =>
    {z | 0 < retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z M}
  have hU : ∀ M, IsOpen (U M) := fun M =>
    isOpen_lt continuous_const (continuous_retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q M)
  have hcover : S ⊆ ⋃ M, U M := by
    intro z hz
    have hn : ‖z‖ = 1 := by simpa only [S, mem_sphere, dist_zero_right] using hz
    have hz0 : z ≠ 0 := by intro he; simp [he] at hn
    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := exists_positive_retainedPrimeFieldPairing Q z hz0
    exact mem_iUnion.mpr ⟨M, hM⟩
  obtain ⟨K, hKcover⟩ := hS.elim_finite_subcover U hU hcover
  have hK : K.Nonempty := by
    obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hSne
    obtain ⟨M, hM, _⟩ := mem_iUnion₂.mp (hKcover hz)
    exact ⟨M, hM⟩
  let F : retainedPrimeFieldCoordinates Q → ℝ := fun z =>

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RetainedPrimeMobiusEulerIdentity
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.MobiusHalfSelectionPoleObstruction

/-!
# Exact retained source and its divisor convolution

The full retained weighted source is the square-root Abel mean of its exact
Dirichlet convolution with the literal divisor increment. Möbius inversion
identifies the infinite series with the completed prime--polar--Gamma source.
The normalized series equals the finite Mellin expression on `Re s > 2`.
This module does not assert its integral representation or source-cone fullness.
-/

noncomputable section
open Complex Finset Filter Topology
open scoped BigOperators
namespace RHTower

/-- The literal retained-functional coefficient as an arithmetic function. -/
def retainedPrimeMobiusAF (P : Finset ℕ) (y : Finset ℕ → ℂ) : ArithmeticFunction ℂ :=
  ⟨retainedPrimeMobiusCoefficient P y, retainedPrimeMobiusCoefficient_zero P y⟩

/-- Complete convolution with the actual prime-free divisor increment. -/
def retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution (P : Finset ℕ) (y : Finset ℕ → ℂ) : ArithmeticFunction ℂ :=
  retainedPrimeMobiusAF P y * halfSelectionDivisorSourceAF

private lemma summable_divisor_source {s : ℂ} (hs : 3 / 2 < s.re) :
    LSeriesSummable halfSelectionDivisorSourceAF s := by
  apply (LSeriesSummable_congr s (fun {n} hn => halfSelectionDivisorSourceAF_apply hn)).mpr
  exact LSeriesSummable_primeFreeDivisorIncrement hs

/-- Absolute convergence of the complete retained convolution on a safe half-plane. -/
lemma LSeriesSummable_retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution (P : Finset ℕ) (y : Finset ℕ → ℂ)
    {s : ℂ} (hs : 3 / 2 < s.re) :
    LSeriesSummable (retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution P y) s :=
  ArithmeticFunction.LSeriesSummable_mul
    (LSeriesSummable_retainedPrimeMobiusCoefficient P y (by linarith)) (summable_divisor_source hs)

/-- Complete L-series product of the literal weighted source and divisor increment. -/
lemma LSeries_retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution_eq_product (P : Finset ℕ) (y : Finset ℕ → ℂ)
    {s : ℂ} (hs : 3 / 2 < s.re) :
    LSeries (retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution P y) s =
      LSeries (retainedPrimeMobiusCoefficient P y) s * divisorSourceDirichlet s := by
  rw [retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution, ArithmeticFunction.LSeries_mul'
    (f := retainedPrimeMobiusAF P y) (g := halfSelectionDivisorSourceAF)
    (LSeriesSummable_retainedPrimeMobiusCoefficient P y (by linarith)) (summable_divisor_source hs),
    divisorSourceDirichlet_eq_LSeries hs]
  congr 1
  exact LSeries_congr (fun {n} hn => halfSelectionDivisorSourceAF_apply hn) s

private lemma sum_divisor_source (N : ℕ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 N, halfSelectionDivisorSourceAF n) = (primeFreeDivisorDefect N : ℂ) := by
  rw [← sum_primeFreeDivisorIncrement N, Complex.ofReal_sum]
  apply sum_congr rfl
  intro n hn
  exact halfSelectionDivisorSourceAF_apply (by have := (mem_Icc.mp hn).1; omega)

/-- The convolution's summatory function is the exact retained floor-dilation source. -/
lemma sum_retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution (P : Finset ℕ) (y : Finset ℕ → ℂ) (N : ℕ) :
    (∑ n ∈ Icc 1 N, retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution P y n) =
      ∑ d ∈ Icc 1 N, retainedPrimeMobiusCoefficient P y d * (primeFreeDivisorDefect (N / d) : ℂ) := by
  rw [retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution, sum_Icc_mul_apply]
  simp_rw [sum_divisor_source]
  rfl

/-- Actual source pairing with a functional on all retained prime subsets. -/
def retainedPrimeSourceMean (P : Finset ℕ) (y : Finset ℕ → ℂ) (M : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ d ∈ Icc 1 M, y (d.primeFactors ∩ P) * (mobiusDivisorDilationChannel M d : ℂ)

/-- The literal source pairing is the exact square-root Abel mean of the
complete convolution, including every clipped endpoint. -/
lemma retainedPrimeSourceMean_eq_convolution_abel (P : Finset ℕ) (y : Finset ℕ → ℂ) (M : ℕ) :
    retainedPrimeSourceMean P y M =
      ∑ k ∈ Icc 1 (M - 1), ((Real.sqrt (k + 1 : ℕ) - Real.sqrt k : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ∑ n ∈ Icc 1 k, retainedPrimeDivisorConvolution P y n := by
  have hlast : mobiusDivisorDilationChannel M M = 0 := by
    by_cases hM : M = 0
    · subst M
      simp [mobiusDivisorDilationChannel]
    · simp [mobiusDivisorDilationChannel, Icc_eq_empty_of_lt (by omega : M - 1 < M)]
  have hdrop : (∑ d ∈ Icc 1 (M - 1),
      y (d.primeFactors ∩ P) * (mobiusDivisorDilationChannel M d : ℂ)) =
      retainedPrimeSourceMean P y M := by
    apply sum_subset
    · intro d hd
      obtain ⟨hl, hu⟩ := mem_Icc.mp hd
      exact mem_Icc.mpr ⟨hl, by omega⟩
    · intro d hd hn
      have he : d = M := by simp only [mem_Icc] at hd hn; omega
      subst d
      simp only [hlast, Complex.ofReal_zero, mul_zero]
  have hpoint (d : ℕ) : y (d.primeFactors ∩ P) * (mobiusDivisorDilationChannel M d : ℂ) =
      ∑ k ∈ Icc d (M - 1), ((Real.sqrt (k + 1 : ℕ) - Real.sqrt k : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        (retainedPrimeMobiusCoefficient P y d * (primeFreeDivisorDefect (k / d) : ℂ)) := by
    rw [mobiusDivisorDilationChannel, Complex.ofReal_mul, Complex.ofReal_sum,
      Finset.mul_sum, Finset.mul_sum]

/-!
# Terminal contact charge of the adaptive mixed arithmetic source

The all-degree adaptive mixed/completed `P^sharp` source reserve has one distinguished final
summand.  Removing that summand leaves a retained reserve, while the literal source action itself
defines a terminal charge before any reflection or observation map is applied.  In every positive
right chamber this charge is exactly

`4 (N + 1) beta_(N+1) = 4 (N + 1) h_(N+1) / h_N`.

At a strict shifted-Xi frontier the numerator is precisely the newborn admission norm.  Hence an
arbitrary finite first contact of order `d` lands in this source channel with an exact positive
order-`d` residue.  The other reserve terms are retained rather than being asked to report the
contact.
-/

open Filter Matrix Polynomial Set Topology
open scoped BigOperators

namespace RHTower
namespace XiShiftedCanonicalAdmission

noncomputable section

/-- All all-degree source reserve except the newborn terminal Jacobi mass. -/
noncomputable def xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeRetainedSourceReserve
    (y : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N,
      (HTGeometry.monicOrthoAlpha
          (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) j -
        HTGeometry.monicOrthoAlpha
          (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) (j + 1)) ^ 2) +
    2 * HTGeometry.monicOrthoAlpha
        (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) 0 ^ 2 +
    8 * (∑ j ∈ Finset.range N,
      HTGeometry.monicOrthoBeta
        (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) j) +
    4 * (N + 1 : ℝ) *
      HTGeometry.monicOrthoBeta
        (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) N

/-- Source-first terminal channel left after the literal top source pays every lower connector and
the retained reserve.  This is defined from the adaptive mixed/completed source action, not from a
Jacobi coordinate or a reporting functional. -/
noncomputable def xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveMixedTerminalSourceCharge
    (w : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  2 * xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveMixedCompletedSourceAction w N -
    xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeConnectorEnergy (w ^ 2) N -
    xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeRetainedSourceReserve (w ^ 2) N

/-- Exact, unconditional accounting identity defining the terminal channel inside the literal
source aggregate. -/
theorem two_mul_adaptiveMixedCompletedSourceAction_eq_connector_add_retained_add_terminalCharge
    (w : ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    2 * xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveMixedCompletedSourceAction w N =
      xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeConnectorEnergy (w ^ 2) N +
        xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeRetainedSourceReserve (w ^ 2) N +
        xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveMixedTerminalSourceCharge w N := by
  rw [xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveMixedTerminalSourceCharge]
  ring

/-- The previous all-degree reserve is retained reserve plus exactly one newborn Jacobi mass. -/
theorem allDegreeSourceReserve_eq_retained_add_terminalBeta
    (y : ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeSourceReserve y N =
      xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeRetainedSourceReserve y N +
        4 * (N + 1 : ℝ) *
          HTGeometry.monicOrthoBeta
            (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) (N + 1) := by
  rw [xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeSourceReserve,
    xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAllDegreeRetainedSourceReserve]
  ring

/-- **Arithmetic source law for the terminal channel.**  In a positive source chamber, the part
of the literal adaptive mixed/completed aggregate not spent on lower connectors or retained
reserve is exactly weighted newborn Jacobi mass. -/
theorem adaptiveMixedTerminalSourceCharge_eq_terminalBeta
    {w : ℝ} (hw : 1 / 2 < w) {N : ℕ} (hN : 0 < N)
    (hH : (HTGeometry.momentHankelMatrix
      (xiShiftedRealMomentSequence w) (N + 2)).PosDef) :
    xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveMixedTerminalSourceCharge w N =
      4 * (N + 1 : ℝ) *
        HTGeometry.monicOrthoBeta
          (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment (w ^ 2) k).re) (N + 1) := by
  rw [xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdaptiveMixedTerminalSourceCharge,
    two_mul_adaptiveMixedCompletedSourceAction_eq_allDegreeConnectorEnergy_add_reserve
      hw hN hH,
    allDegreeSourceReserve_eq_retained_add_terminalBeta]
  ring

/-- The norm-ratio/Jacobi-edge identification needs only the leading solve block.  No following
positive extension is required. -/
theorem xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdjacentEdge_eq_monicOrthoBeta_of_head_posDef
    {y : ℝ} {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
    (hH : (HTGeometry.momentHankelMatrix
      (fun k => (xiShiftedReciprocalMoment y k).re) n).PosDef) :
    xiShiftedCanonicalAdmissionAdjacentEdge y n =
      HTGeometry.monicOrthoBeta

import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.RetainedPrimeLandauCarrier
import GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower.FiniteDirichletMellinContinuationObstruction

/-!
# Unconditional directional separation of finite retained sources

A one-sided actual retained functional gives a finite positive integral carrier.
Landau transfer reconstructs its Mellin transform analytically on `Re s > 3/4`.
The exact source germ and surviving simple critical poles force every retained
coordinate of that functional to vanish. Every nonzero retained direction
therefore has actual integer cutoffs with both strict signs. No source-sign,
RH or zero-location assumption is added to the resulting witness theorems.
-/

noncomputable section
open Complex MeasureTheory Filter Set ProbabilityTheory Topology
open scoped NNReal
namespace RHTower

/-- The closed low-height balls force every exponential moment they reach for
a one-sided retained functional. -/
lemma retainedPrimeLandau_integrable_transfer
    {Q : Finset Nat.Primes} {y : Finset ℕ → ℝ}
    (h : RetainedPrimeSourceNonnegative Q y) {R : NNReal} (hR : (R : ℝ) < 7 / 2)
    {t : ℝ} (ht0 : 0 ≤ t) (htR : t < (R : ℝ)) :
    Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (t * Real.log x)) (retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y) := by
  apply landau_complexMGF_integrable_transfer
    (log_nonneg_ae_retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y)
    (zero_mem_interior_integrableExpSet_retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y)
    (G := retainedPrimeLandauContinuation Q y) (R := R) _
    (retainedPrimeLandauContinuation_eventuallyEq_complexMGF h) ht0 htR
  exact differentiableOn_finiteDirichletDivisorMellin_landau_ball _
    (retainedPrimeDirichletCoefficients_zero _ _) Q _ hR

lemma Iio_subset_interior_integrableExpSet_retainedPrimeLandauMeasure
    {Q : Finset Nat.Primes} {y : Finset ℕ → ℝ}
    (h : RetainedPrimeSourceNonnegative Q y) {R : NNReal} (hR : (R : ℝ) < 7 / 2) :
    Iio (R : ℝ) ⊆ interior (integrableExpSet Real.log (retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y)) := by
  have hset : Iio (R : ℝ) ⊆ integrableExpSet Real.log (retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y) := by
    intro t ht
    by_cases ht0 : 0 ≤ t
    · exact retainedPrimeLandau_integrable_transfer h hR ht0 ht
    · exact integrable_exp_log_retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y (by linarith)
  intro t ht
  rw [mem_interior_iff_mem_nhds]
  exact mem_of_superset (Iio_mem_nhds ht) hset

/-- A one-sided functional reconstructs an analytic source Mellin transform
past the real part of every surviving critical pole. -/
lemma analyticOnNhd_retainedPrimeLandauReconstruction
    {Q : Finset Nat.Primes} {y : Finset ℕ → ℝ}
    (h : RetainedPrimeSourceNonnegative Q y) :
    AnalyticOnNhd ℂ
      (fun s : ℂ => complexMGF Real.log (retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y) (4 - s))
      {s : ℂ | 3 / 4 < s.re} := by
  let R : NNReal := ⟨13 / 4, by norm_num⟩
  have hinter := Iio_subset_interior_integrableExpSet_retainedPrimeLandauMeasure
    h (R := R) (by change (13 / 4 : ℝ) < 7 / 2; norm_num)
  intro s hs
  change 3 / 4 < s.re at hs
  have hz : (4 - s).re ∈ interior (integrableExpSet Real.log (retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y)) := by
    apply hinter
    change (4 - s).re < 13 / 4
    simp only [sub_re]
    norm_num
    linarith [hs]
  have houter := analyticOnNhd_complexMGF (X := Real.log) (μ := retainedPrimeLandauMeasure Q y)
    (4 - s) hz
  have hshift : AnalyticAt ℂ (fun z : ℂ => 4 - z) s := by fun_prop
  simpa only [Function.comp_def] using houter.comp hshift

/-- Every nonnegative complete retained-source functional vanishes on every
retained coordinate. The conclusion is unconditional and uses actual source values. -/
theorem retainedPrimeSourceNonnegative_coordinates_zero
    {Q : Finset Nat.Primes} {y : Finset ℕ → ℝ}
    (h : RetainedPrimeSourceNonnegative Q y) :
    ∀ R : Finset ℕ, R ⊆ Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ)) → y R = 0 := by
  intro R hR
  by_contra hyR
  let P := Q.image (fun p : Nat.Primes => (p : ℕ))
  have hP : ∀ p ∈ P, p.Prime := by
    intro p hp
    obtain ⟨q, hq, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hp

/-!
# Moments of a scaled mollifier

For `ρ_ε(t) = ε⁻¹ ρ(t/ε)` the first-moment kernel is `k_ε(t) = (t/ε) ρ(t/ε)`, so it is the *same*
profile read at scale `ε`.  Two consequences, which are the card's `(20)`:

* its mass scales, `‖k_ε‖₁ = ε ‖k₁‖₁`, so it vanishes as the mollifier concentrates;
* its derivative's mass does **not**, `‖k_ε′‖₁ = ‖k₁′‖₁`, because the `ε⁻¹` from differentiating and
  the `ε` from the substitution cancel.

That pairing — a vanishing zero-order defect against a bounded first-order one — is what makes the
mollified equation converge without losing the derivative term.
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- The mollifier `ρ` read at scale `ε`. -/
noncomputable def scaledMollifier (ρ : ℝ → ℝ) (ε : ℝ) (t : ℝ) : ℝ := ε⁻¹ * ρ (t / ε)

/-- The derivative of the first-moment kernel `u ↦ u ρ(u)`. -/
noncomputable def firstMomentDeriv (ρ ρ' : ℝ → ℝ) (u : ℝ) : ℝ := ρ u + u * ρ' u

theorem integral_scaledMollifier {ρ : ℝ → ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    (∫ t, scaledMollifier ρ ε t) = ∫ u, ρ u := by
  unfold scaledMollifier
  rw [integral_const_mul, Measure.integral_comp_div ρ ε, abs_of_pos hε, smul_eq_mul, ← mul_assoc,
    inv_mul_cancel₀ hε.ne', one_mul]

  rw [firstMomentKernel, firstMomentKernel, scaledMollifier, ← mul_assoc]

    funext t
    rw [firstMomentKernel_scaled]
  rw [hrw, Measure.integral_comp_div (fun u => |firstMomentKernel ρ u|) ε, abs_of_pos hε,
    smul_eq_mul]

    HasDerivAt (firstMomentKernel ρ) (firstMomentDeriv ρ ρ' u) u := by

  rw [firstMomentDeriv]

    (hρ : ∀ u, HasDerivAt ρ (ρ' u) u) (t : ℝ) :

    (hasDerivAt_firstMomentKernel hρ (t / ε)).comp t hb

      (firstMomentDeriv ρ ρ' (t / ε) * ε⁻¹) t := hcomp0
  refine hcomp.congr_deriv ?_
  ring

invariant: the `ε⁻¹` from differentiating cancels the `ε` from the substitution. -/
theorem integral_abs_firstMomentDeriv_scaled {ρ ρ' : ℝ → ℝ} {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    (∫ t, |ε⁻¹ * firstMomentDeriv ρ ρ' (t / ε)|)
      = ∫ u, |firstMomentDeriv ρ ρ' u| := by
  have hrw : (fun t => |ε⁻¹ * firstMomentDeriv ρ ρ' (t / ε)|)

    funext t

/-!
# The derivative along the second null coordinate

The first null coordinate is differentiated by the fundamental theorem of calculus applied to the
outer integral. The second one sits inside that integral, so differentiating it is the Leibniz rule:
the inner integral has the integrand as its derivative in its own upper limit, and the data are
continuous on the whole plane once the null coordinates are clamped, so no domination hypothesis has
to be checked.

Differentiating the result once more in the first null coordinate returns the step operator, so the
mixed derivative is the same in both orders, as the equality of the two continuous mixed partials
requires. That symmetric pair is what the chart d'Alembertian consumes.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

open Set Complex Metric

open scoped Interval

/-- The inner integral of the clamped step is jointly continuous in its upper limit and in the
other null coordinate. -/
theorem continuous_clampedInnerSnd {ρ₀ Mv ρ T : ℝ} (hρ₀ : 0 < ρ₀) {V : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ → ℂ}
    (hV : StripPotential V ρ₀)
    (hMv0 : 0 ≤ Mv)
    (hMv : ∀ s t : ℝ, |s| ≤ T → |t| ≤ T → ∀ z ∈ imStrip ρ₀, ‖V s t z‖ ≤ Mv)
    (hρ0 : 0 ≤ ρ) (hρ : ρ < ρ₀) (hT : 0 ≤ T)
    (hsmall : (4 + Mv * ρ₀ ^ 2 / 4) * T ^ 2 * Real.exp 2 / ((ρ₀ - ρ) / 2) ^ 2 < 1)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| ≤ ρ) :
    Continuous fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..p.1, clampedStep V T z p.2 t := by
  have hFc := continuous_clampedStep hρ₀ hV hMv0 hMv hρ0 hρ hT hsmall hz
  have huncurry : Continuous fun q : (ℝ × ℝ) × ℝ => clampedStep V T z q.1.2 q.2 :=
    hFc.comp (f := fun q : (ℝ × ℝ) × ℝ => ((q.1.2, q.2) : ℝ × ℝ))
      ((continuous_snd.comp continuous_fst).prodMk continuous_snd)
  exact intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous
    (f := fun (p : ℝ × ℝ) (t : ℝ) => clampedStep V T z p.2 t) huncurry continuous_fst

Purpose: discriminate mechanisms at open source gates after surveying all 25 live labels and 35 candidate labels in the frontier, its six primitive gates, and the universal-law constraints. The focused central Hankel proof attempt is paused. No experiment is a proof of RH.

Method: follow `docs/meta/scientific-method.md`. Freeze each experimental hypothesis before evaluation, seek hostile counterexamples, compare with matched controls, and keep any surviving claim distinct from a proved bridge. These are mechanism probes; no new universal primitive or universal law is claimed before the observations justify one. A later primary conjecture must pass the guide's shadow and distance gates.

## E: how an added integer block changes Möbius energy

Corpus inputs: exact Gamma--Hankel/Laplace identity (`MobiusLaplaceGammaHankelWall`), divisibility-supported source births, and confinement of possible escape to a moving cusp (`MobiusIntegerCuspConfinement`). Positivity of energy supplies no upper ceiling. A bounded-return subsequence could feed the existing Mellin/Plancherel endpoint.

**Frozen H1:** For every dyadic `N≥256` and `1.01≤r≤1.5`, the cross energy between the literal Möbius prefix `[1,N]` and its next block `(N,2N]` is nonpositive:

`C_r(N)=Γ(r) Σ_(m≤N<n≤2N) μ(m)μ(n)/(m+n)^r ≤ 0`.

Meaning: new arithmetic coefficients oppose rather than reinforce the old energy. It is suggested by the need for cancellation at source births, not implied by any existing energy or cusp theorem. A positive cross value falsifies this strong local mechanism. It does not disprove a recurrent or collective mechanism, nor RH.

Probe dyadic cutoffs through `2^17`, several fixed `r`, signs and magnitudes of `C`, and the exact balance `E_(2N)=E_N+E_block+2C`. Controls preserve squarefree support: independent sign shuffles within dyadic shells and random multiplicative prime signs. They distinguish literal Möbius structure from sparsity and multiplicativity alone. Use FFT convolution for all additive correlations; independently verify selected integrals in the logarithmic Laplace coordinate. Target <120 seconds per batch.

## O/P: pairwise versus collective prime interference

Corpus inputs: individual outer-prime norm saturation despite pole constraints; strict two-prime norm subadditivity (`CCMRestrictedWeilPrimeInterference`); and full ground positivity still open. Prior ground-energy scans are not repeated.

**Frozen H2:** Pairwise coalitions recover at least half the collective norm saving of the positive weighted outer-prime transport, over apertures `1≤a≤3`. In each finite Legendre compression, define the full saving as `Σ||T_p||-||ΣT_p||`; compare it with the best saving achievable by a partition into pairs and singletons.

Meaning: two-prime incompatibility is the dominant mechanism. A verified finite compression where even the optimal pairing recovers less than half falsifies the compression version. Positive outcomes do not establish the operator statement. Compare basis sizes and actual prime locations with a mass-preserving evenly spaced location control. The quantity being probed is collective structure, not the expected sign of a Weil ground energy. Target <120 seconds.

## CLG/TTF: does tail mass determine the surviving compensation sign?

Corpus inputs: full theta likelihood has an atomic-plus-ray positive spectral measure; the four-face positive cone is formally false; the combined third homotopy compensation survives earlier literal-source tests. Remaining compact source sign still needs a mechanism.

**Frozen H3:** On the structural tail, nonnegativity of the third compensation derivative survives replacing the higher theta likelihood measure by a positive one- or two-atom measure on `[3,∞)` with exactly the same Laplace mass at the left evaluation point `u-t`.

Meaning: total tail mass and its spectral gap, rather than the detailed arithmetic distribution, suffice for this sign. Controls leave the first-atom background fixed and change only the higher-tail measure. This is a risky hypothesis: mass preservation does not preserve higher likelihood moments. Record the first violating configuration and its jets; verify it at increased precision. If false, inspect which coupled moment becomes decisive instead of adding assumptions to rescue H3. This is a probe of a CLG source subproblem, not the paused central Hankel problem. Target <120 seconds.

/-!
# The prime-log jump shell and its essential-phase packet

For `0 < A < B` the *jump shell* is the indicator of the symmetric annulus `A < |x| < B`; it is the
difference of the two normalized interval windows exposed by dividing a theta translation anomaly by
the Xi conormal at two distinct primes, with `A = (log p)/2` and `B = (log q)/2`.

Modulating the shell by a cosine and subtracting the shell average produces the *essential-phase
jump packet*

```text
u_κ(x) = 1_{A<|x|<B}(x) · (cos (κ x) − μ_κ),
μ_κ = (sin (κ B) − sin (κ A)) / (κ (B − A)),
```

an even, compactly supported, real function, vanishing at the origin and of zero mean — an exact
two-condition Poisson source test in the jump class rather than the smooth class.  As `κ → ∞` the
correction `μ_κ` vanishes and the squared norm tends to the shell half-width `B − A`.
-/

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

open MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

/-- The symmetric annulus `A < |x| < B`, as the union of the two intervals it consists of. -/
def jumpShellSet (A B : ℝ) : Set ℝ := Ioo (-B) (-A) ∪ Ioo A B

theorem measurableSet_jumpShellSet (A B : ℝ) : MeasurableSet (jumpShellSet A B) :=
  (measurableSet_Ioo).union measurableSet_Ioo

theorem mem_jumpShellSet_iff {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (x : ℝ) :
    x ∈ jumpShellSet A B ↔ A < |x| ∧ |x| < B := by
  constructor
  · rintro (⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩)
    · have hx : x < 0 := by linarith
      rw [abs_of_neg hx]
      constructor <;> linarith
    · have hx : 0 < x := by linarith
      rw [abs_of_pos hx]
      exact ⟨h1, h2⟩
  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
    rcases lt_trichotomy x 0 with hx | hx | hx
    · left
      rw [abs_of_neg hx] at h1 h2
      constructor <;> linarith
    · exfalso
      rw [hx] at h1
      simp at h1
      linarith
    · right
      rw [abs_of_pos hx] at h1 h2
      exact ⟨h1, h2⟩

theorem jumpShellSet_disjoint {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) :
    Disjoint (Ioo (-B) (-A)) (Ioo A B) := by
  rw [Set.disjoint_left]
  rintro x ⟨-, hx⟩ ⟨hx', -⟩
  linarith

/-- The jump shell: the indicator function of the annulus. -/
noncomputable def jumpShell (A B : ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ := (jumpShellSet A B).indicator 1

theorem jumpShell_neg {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (x : ℝ) :
    jumpShell A B (-x) = jumpShell A B x := by
  classical
  simp only [jumpShell, Set.indicator_apply]
  by_cases hx : x ∈ jumpShellSet A B
  · have : -x ∈ jumpShellSet A B := by
      rw [mem_jumpShellSet_iff hA] at hx ⊢
      simpa using hx
    simp [hx, this]
  · have : -x ∉ jumpShellSet A B := by
      rw [mem_jumpShellSet_iff hA] at hx ⊢
      simpa using hx
    simp [hx, this]

theorem jumpShell_zero {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) : jumpShell A B 0 = 0 := by
  classical
  have h0 : (0 : ℝ) ∉ jumpShellSet A B := by
    rw [mem_jumpShellSet_iff hA]
    rintro ⟨h1, -⟩
    rw [abs_zero] at h1
    linarith
  simp [jumpShell, h0]

/-- The shell average of the modulating cosine. -/
noncomputable def jumpMean (A B κ : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (Real.sin (κ * B) - Real.sin (κ * A)) / (κ * (B - A))

/-- The essential-phase jump packet. -/
noncomputable def jumpPacket (A B κ : ℝ) : ℝ → ℝ :=
  fun x => jumpShell A B x * (Real.cos (κ * x) - jumpMean A B κ)

theorem jumpPacket_neg {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (κ x : ℝ) :
    jumpPacket A B κ (-x) = jumpPacket A B κ x := by
  simp only [jumpPacket, jumpShell_neg hA]
  rw [show κ * -x = -(κ * x) by ring, Real.cos_neg]

theorem jumpPacket_zero {A B : ℝ} (hA : 0 < A) (κ : ℝ) : jumpPacket A B κ 0 = 0 := by
  simp [jumpPacket, jumpShell_zero hA]

/-! ### The shell integrals -/

section Integrals

variable {A B κ : ℝ}

theorem integrableOn_jumpShellSet {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) (hA : 0 < A) (_hAB : A < B) :
    IntegrableOn f (jumpShellSet A B) := by
  have h1 : IntegrableOn f (Icc (-B) B) := hf.integrableOn_Icc
  refine h1.mono_set ?_
  rintro x (⟨h1, h2⟩ | ⟨h1, h2⟩) <;> constructor <;> linarith

theorem integrable_jumpShell_mul {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) (hA : 0 < A) (hAB : A < B) :
    Integrable (fun x => jumpShell A B x * f x) := by
  classical
  have h1 : (fun x => jumpShell A B x * f x) = (jumpShellSet A B).indicator f := by
    funext x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ jumpShellSet A B <;> simp [jumpShell, hx]
  rw [h1]
  exact (integrableOn_jumpShellSet hf hA hAB).integrable_indicator
    (measurableSet_jumpShellSet A B)

theorem integral_jumpShell_mul (hA : 0 < A) (hAB : A < B) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Continuous f) :
    ∫ x, jumpShell A B x * f x = (∫ x in (-B)..(-A), f x) + ∫ x in A..B, f x := by
  classical
  have h1 : (fun x => jumpShell A B x * f x) = (jumpShellSet A B).indicator f := by
    funext x
    by_cases hx : x ∈ jumpShellSet A B <;> simp [jumpShell, hx]
  have hint : ∀ a b : ℝ, IntegrableOn f (Ioo a b) := by
    intro a b
    exact (hf.integrableOn_Icc (a := a) (b := b)).mono_set Ioo_subset_Icc_self
  have hIoo : ∀ a b : ℝ, a ≤ b → ∫ x in Ioo a b, f x = ∫ x in a..b, f x := by
    intro a b hab
    rw [intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hab, MeasureTheory.integral_Ioc_eq_integral_Ioo]

/-!
# Local expansion of the boundary packet modulus

At infinitesimal separation the two-point modulus of the boundary complementary packet is governed
by the jump structure of its kernel rather than by its cofinal slope.  The kernel

```text
k_ω(t) = e^(-(1+ω)t) ∑_{m ≤ e^t} m^ω − 1/(1+ω)
```

is smooth off the discrete set `{log m : m ≥ 2}` and jumps by `1/m` at `log m`; the swept branch of
the modulus carries the remaining unit jump at the origin.  Each jump of size `j` contributes
`j² a + O(a²)` to the modulus at separation `a`, so

```text
lim_{a → 0+} D_ω(a) / a = ∑_{m ≥ 1} 1/m² = π²/6 .
```

Since `π²/6 > 1`, the packet is **locally expansive**: no pointwise contraction `D_ω(a) ≤ a` holds
near zero.  The successful metric law is the cofinal one of `ComplementaryPacketCofinalIsometry`,
not this local one.

The proof is an explicit two-region estimate.  On `(0, log N)` the translation window meets at most
one jump once `a ≤ 1/(2(N+1))`, which linearises the square of the increment; beyond `log N` the
increment is controlled by the counting function `⌊e^(r+a)⌋ − ⌊e^r⌋`, whose exponentially weighted
integral is `O(a/N)`.
-/

noncomputable section

/-! ### The step profile and the increment identity -/

/-- The step profile of the boundary packet: the power sum truncated at `e^t`. -/
def packetStepSum (ω t : ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (⌊Real.exp t⌋₊ + 1), (i : ℝ) ^ ω

theorem complementaryPacketKernel_add_const (ω : ℝ) (hω : 0 ≤ ω) (t : ℝ) :
    complementaryPacketKernel ω t + complementaryPacketConstant ω
      = Real.exp (-(1 + ω) * t) * packetStepSum ω t := by
  rw [complementaryPacketKernel_eq ω hω t, complementaryPacketConstant, packetStepSum]
  ring

theorem packetStepSum_sub (ω : ℝ) {t s : ℝ} (hts : t ≤ s) :
    packetStepSum ω s - packetStepSum ω t
      = ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico (⌊Real.exp t⌋₊ + 1) (⌊Real.exp s⌋₊ + 1), (i : ℝ) ^ ω := by
  have hle : ⌊Real.exp t⌋₊ + 1 ≤ ⌊Real.exp s⌋₊ + 1 :=
    Nat.succ_le_succ (Nat.floor_mono (Real.exp_le_exp.mpr hts))
  rw [Finset.sum_Ico_eq_sub _ hle]
  rfl

/-- The jump mass swept by a translation of size `a` at clock time `r`. -/
def packetJump (ω a r : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (-(1 + ω) * (r + a)) *
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico (⌊Real.exp r⌋₊ + 1) (⌊Real.exp (r + a)⌋₊ + 1), (i : ℝ) ^ ω

/-- **Increment identity.**  The packet increment splits into the jump mass swept by the
translation and an exponential drift of the incoming profile. -/
theorem complementaryPacketKernel_sub_eq (ω : ℝ) (hω : 0 ≤ ω) (r : ℝ) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    complementaryPacketKernel ω (r + a) - complementaryPacketKernel ω r
      = packetJump ω a r
        + (Real.exp (-(1 + ω) * a) - 1) *
            (complementaryPacketKernel ω r + complementaryPacketConstant ω) := by
  have hE : Real.exp (-(1 + ω) * (r + a))
      = Real.exp (-(1 + ω) * a) * Real.exp (-(1 + ω) * r) := by
    rw [← Real.exp_add]
    ring_nf
  have h1 := complementaryPacketKernel_add_const ω hω (r + a)
  have h2 := complementaryPacketKernel_add_const ω hω r
  have hgoal : complementaryPacketKernel ω (r + a) - complementaryPacketKernel ω r
      = (complementaryPacketKernel ω (r + a) + complementaryPacketConstant ω)
        - (complementaryPacketKernel ω r + complementaryPacketConstant ω) := by ring
  rw [packetJump, hgoal, ← packetStepSum_sub ω (show r ≤ r + a by linarith), h1, h2, hE]
  ring

/-! ### Pointwise bounds -/

private theorem rpow_two_le_two {ω : ℝ} (hω : ω ≤ 1) : (2 : ℝ) ^ ω ≤ 2 := by
  calc (2 : ℝ) ^ ω ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (1 : ℝ) := Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_le (by norm_num) hω
    _ = 2 := Real.rpow_one 2

private theorem abs_sub_le_abs_add_abs (x y : ℝ) : |x - y| ≤ |x| + |y| := by
  calc |x - y| = |x + -y| := by ring_nf
    _ ≤ |x| + |-y| := abs_add_le _ _
    _ = |x| + |y| := by rw [abs_neg]

theorem abs_packetIncomingProfile_le {ω : ℝ} (hω0 : 0 ≤ ω) (hω : ω ≤ 1 / 2) {r : ℝ}
    (hr : 0 ≤ r) :
    |complementaryPacketKernel ω r + complementaryPacketConstant ω| ≤ 3 := by
  have henv := abs_complementaryPacketKernel_le ω hω0 hr
  have h2ω : (2 : ℝ) ^ ω ≤ 2 := rpow_two_le_two (by linarith)
  have h2ω0 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ ω := Real.rpow_nonneg (by norm_num) ω
  have hexp0 : (0 : ℝ) < Real.exp (-r) := Real.exp_pos _
  have hexp : Real.exp (-r) ≤ 1 := Real.exp_le_one_iff.mpr (by linarith)
  have hk : |complementaryPacketKernel ω r| ≤ 2 := by
    refine henv.trans ?_
    nlinarith
  have hc : |complementaryPacketConstant ω| ≤ 1 := by
    rw [complementaryPacketConstant, abs_of_nonneg (by positivity)]
    rw [div_le_one (by linarith)]
    linarith
  calc |complementaryPacketKernel ω r + complementaryPacketConstant ω|
      ≤ |complementaryPacketKernel ω r| + |complementaryPacketConstant ω| := abs_add_le _ _
    _ ≤ 3 := by linarith

/-!
# The atomic jump form of a translation pair

A symmetric translation pair is not arbitrary forcing: the finite-difference Dirichlet form

`J_h(u, φ) = ∫ (u(x+h) − u(x)) (φ(x+h) − φ(x)) dx`

equals `2⟨u, φ⟩ − ⟨u(·+h), φ⟩ − ⟨u(·−h), φ⟩`, so a symmetric pair of translations is a positive
atomic Dirichlet form minus twice the identity.  Against a one-Lipschitz increasing truncation the
form is coercive: `J_h(u, T u) ≥ J_h(T u, T u) ≥ 0`.  Both statements are proved here for
continuous compactly supported data, and the von Mangoldt weights `Λ(n)/√n` are nonnegative, so a
finite positive combination of translation pairs inherits the sign.
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-! ## The jump form -/

/-- Finite-difference Dirichlet form at displacement `h`. -/
noncomputable def jumpForm (h : ℝ) (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∫ x, (u (x + h) - u x) * (φ (x + h) - φ x)

/-- The `L²` pairing. -/
noncomputable def pairing (u φ : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ := ∫ x, u x * φ x

private theorem integrable_shift_mul {u φ : ℝ → ℝ} (hu : Continuous u) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hcu : HasCompactSupport u) (s t : ℝ) :
    Integrable (fun x => u (x + s) * φ (x + t)) := by
  have hcont : Continuous fun x : ℝ => u (x + s) * φ (x + t) :=
    ((hu.comp (continuous_id.add continuous_const)).mul
      (hφ.comp (continuous_id.add continuous_const)))
  refine hcont.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport ?_
  have h1 : HasCompactSupport fun x : ℝ => u (x + s) :=
    hcu.comp_homeomorph (Homeomorph.addRight s)
  exact h1.mul_right

private theorem integral_shift (f : ℝ → ℝ) (s : ℝ) : ∫ x, f (x + s) = ∫ x, f x :=
  integral_add_right_eq_self f s

/-- **Translation-pair identity.**  The jump form is twice the pairing minus the two shifted
pairings, so a symmetric translation pair is a positive atomic Dirichlet form minus twice the
identity. -/
theorem jumpForm_eq_two_pairing_sub {u φ : ℝ → ℝ} (hu : Continuous u) (hφ : Continuous φ)
    (hcu : HasCompactSupport u) (h : ℝ) :
    jumpForm h u φ =
      2 * pairing u φ - pairing (fun x => u (x + h)) φ - pairing (fun x => u (x - h)) φ := by
  have e1 : Integrable (fun x => u (x + h) * φ (x + h)) :=
    integrable_shift_mul hu hφ hcu h h
  have e2 : Integrable (fun x => u (x + h) * φ (x + 0)) :=
    integrable_shift_mul hu hφ hcu h 0
  have e3 : Integrable (fun x => u (x + 0) * φ (x + h)) :=
    integrable_shift_mul hu hφ hcu 0 h
  have e4 : Integrable (fun x => u (x + 0) * φ (x + 0)) :=
    integrable_shift_mul hu hφ hcu 0 0

    have := integral_shift (fun y => u (y - h) * φ y) h

/-- The one-Lipschitz increasing truncation `s ↦ (s − t)⁺`. -/
noncomputable def truncPos (t s : ℝ) : ℝ := max (s - t) 0

theorem truncPos_sub_le (t r s : ℝ) : |truncPos t r - truncPos t s| ≤ |r - s| := by
  simp only [truncPos]
  exact abs_max_sub_max_le_abs _ _ _ |>.trans (by rw [sub_sub_sub_cancel_right])

  max_le_max (by linarith) le_rfl

`(r − s)(T r − T s) ≥ (T r − T s)²`. -/

  rcases le_total s r with hrs | hrs

    have hlip : truncPos t r - truncPos t s ≤ r - s := by
      have := truncPos_sub_le t r s

  · have hmono : truncPos t r ≤ truncPos t s := truncPos_mono t hrs
    have hlip : truncPos t s - truncPos t r ≤ s - r := by
      have := truncPos_sub_le t s r
      rw [abs_le] at this
      have h2 : |s - r| = s - r := abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)
      rw [h2] at this

/-!
# The Gamma jump is a positive operator, in physical space

Pairing the second difference with the profile and integrating over the line turns it into a
squared translation increment:

`∫ [2F(L) − F(L+s) − F(L−s)] F(L) dL = ∫ [F(L+s) − F(L)]² dL`.

Translation invariance of Lebesgue measure is the only input — no Fourier transform, no Plancherel,
no spectral measure.  Integrating against the positive kernel `1/(e^s − 1)` therefore makes the
Gamma jump's quadratic form the weighted total translation energy, hence nonnegative, and gives the
exact identity that the coercive tail estimates consume.
-/

open MeasureTheory

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

section Translation

variable {F : ℝ → ℝ}

theorem integrable_sq_comp_add (hF2 : Integrable (fun L => F L ^ 2)) (c : ℝ) :
    Integrable (fun L => F (L + c) ^ 2) := by
  simpa using hF2.comp_add_right c

theorem integral_sq_comp_add (c : ℝ) :
    (∫ L, F (L + c) ^ 2) = ∫ L, F L ^ 2 :=
  integral_add_right_eq_self (μ := (volume : Measure ℝ)) (fun L => F L ^ 2) c

theorem integrable_translate_mul (hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable F volume)
    (hF2 : Integrable (fun L => F L ^ 2)) (c : ℝ) :
    Integrable (fun L => F (L + c) * F L) := by
  have hmeas' : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun L => F (L + c) * F L) volume :=
    ((hmeas.comp_measurePreserving (measurePreserving_add_right volume c)).mul hmeas)
  refine Integrable.mono' (g := fun L => (F (L + c) ^ 2 + F L ^ 2) / 2) ?_ hmeas' ?_
  · exact ((integrable_sq_comp_add hF2 c).add hF2).div_const 2
  · filter_upwards with L
    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul]
    nlinarith [sq_nonneg (|F (L + c)| - |F L|), sq_abs (F (L + c)), sq_abs (F L)]

/-- Pairing a backward translate with the profile is pairing the profile with a forward
translate. -/
theorem integral_translate_neg_mul (s : ℝ) :
    (∫ L, F (L - s) * F L) = ∫ L, F (L + s) * F L := by
  have h := integral_add_right_eq_self (μ := (volume : Measure ℝ))
    (fun L => F (L - s) * F L) s
  rw [← h]
  refine integral_congr_ae ?_
  filter_upwards with L
  show F (L + s - s) * F (L + s) = F (L + s) * F L
  rw [add_sub_cancel_right, mul_comm]

/-- **The Gamma second difference pairs to a squared translation increment.** -/
theorem integral_secondDifference_mul_self (hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable F volume)
    (hF2 : Integrable (fun L => F L ^ 2)) (s : ℝ) :
    (∫ L, secondDifference F L s * F L) = ∫ L, (F (L + s) - F L) ^ 2 := by
  have hp : Integrable (fun L => F (L + s) * F L) := integrable_translate_mul hmeas hF2 s
  have hm : Integrable (fun L => F (L - s) * F L) := by
    have := integrable_translate_mul hmeas hF2 (-s)
    simpa [sub_eq_add_neg] using this
  have hs2 : Integrable (fun L => F (L + s) ^ 2) := integrable_sq_comp_add hF2 s
  have hlhs : (fun L => secondDifference F L s * F L)
      = fun L => 2 * F L ^ 2 - F (L + s) * F L - F (L - s) * F L := by
    funext L
    rw [secondDifference]
    ring
  have hrhs : (fun L => (F (L + s) - F L) ^ 2)
      = fun L => F (L + s) ^ 2 - 2 * (F (L + s) * F L) + F L ^ 2 := by
    funext L
    ring
  have i1 : (∫ L, 2 * F L ^ 2 - F (L + s) * F L - F (L - s) * F L)
      = (∫ L, 2 * F L ^ 2 - F (L + s) * F L) - ∫ L, F (L - s) * F L :=
    integral_sub ((hF2.const_mul 2).sub hp) hm
  have i2 : (∫ L, 2 * F L ^ 2 - F (L + s) * F L)
      = (∫ L, 2 * F L ^ 2) - ∫ L, F (L + s) * F L :=
    integral_sub (hF2.const_mul 2) hp
  have i3 : (∫ L, 2 * F L ^ 2) = 2 * ∫ L, F L ^ 2 := integral_const_mul 2 _
  have j1 : (∫ L, F (L + s) ^ 2 - 2 * (F (L + s) * F L) + F L ^ 2)
      = (∫ L, F (L + s) ^ 2 - 2 * (F (L + s) * F L)) + ∫ L, F L ^ 2 :=
    integral_add (hs2.sub (hp.const_mul 2)) hF2
  have j2 : (∫ L, F (L + s) ^ 2 - 2 * (F (L + s) * F L))
      = (∫ L, F (L + s) ^ 2) - ∫ L, 2 * (F (L + s) * F L) :=
    integral_sub hs2 (hp.const_mul 2)
  have j3 : (∫ L, 2 * (F (L + s) * F L)) = 2 * ∫ L, F (L + s) * F L := integral_const_mul 2 _
  rw [hlhs, hrhs, i1, i2, i3, j1, j2, j3, integral_translate_neg_mul (F := F) s,
    integral_sq_comp_add (F := F) s]
  ring

/-- **The Gamma jump has nonnegative pairing at every scale.** -/
theorem integral_secondDifference_mul_self_nonneg (hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable F volume)
    (hF2 : Integrable (fun L => F L ^ 2)) (s : ℝ) :
    0 ≤ ∫ L, secondDifference F L s * F L := by
  rw [integral_secondDifference_mul_self hmeas hF2 s]
  exact integral_nonneg fun L => sq_nonneg _

/-! ## The shifted jump and the exact numerical-range constant -/

/-- The exponentially conjugated second difference, `exp(sigma L) R exp(-sigma L)` at scale `s`. -/

/-!
# Gelfand-triple completion of Deninger arithmetic cohomology

Deninger's positive Hodge metric is defined on middle cohomology and its completion is the
Hilbert--Pólya space.  The compact-open quotient and its strong dual therefore occur as the
distribution and test boundaries of a Gelfand triple

`H¹_c ⊂ H¹_Hilb ⊂ H¹_ent`,

not as two spaces which the Hodge star must identify directly.

This file formalizes the exact source-comparison interface for that missing Hilbert completion.
The distribution boundary is the already constructed compact-open Xi quotient; the test boundary
is its strong continuous dual.  A completed arithmetic realization must embed both around a
Hilbert middle space, carry Deninger's closed polarized Frobenius generator, and lift every
source-defined Xi eigenclass into its operator domain.

No instance of this structure is postulated.  Lean proves that constructing one is sufficient for
RH, using the source quotient eigenvectors rather than a divisor-defined Hilbert carrier.
-/

open Complex

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-- Chosen source eigenclass supplied by the compact-open divided-chain construction. -/
def deningerCompactOpenThetaEigenvector
    (rho : XiDivisorSupport) :
    DeningerArithmeticCompactOpenH1 :=
  Classical.choose
    (exists_deningerCompactOpenTheta_eigenvector rho)

/-- The chosen compact-open source eigenclass is nonzero. -/
theorem deningerCompactOpenThetaEigenvector_ne_zero
    (rho : XiDivisorSupport) :
    deningerCompactOpenThetaEigenvector rho ≠ 0 :=
  (Classical.choose_spec
    (exists_deningerCompactOpenTheta_eigenvector rho)).1

/-- The chosen source class has the exact Xi Frobenius eigenvalue. -/
theorem deningerCompactOpenThetaEigenvector_eigen
    (rho : XiDivisorSupport) :
    deningerCompactOpenTheta
        (deningerCompactOpenThetaEigenvector rho) =
      (1 / 2 + Complex.I * xiSpectralPointSupport rho) •
        deningerCompactOpenThetaEigenvector rho :=
  (Classical.choose_spec
    (exists_deningerCompactOpenTheta_eigenvector rho)).2

/--
A complex-linear test embedding cannot realize the ordinary continuous-dual pairing through
mathlib's conjugate-linear-first Hilbert product: scalar multiplication by `I` forces every such
pairing to vanish.  This is why the genuine Gelfand test embedding below is conjugate-linear.
-/
theorem deningerLinearTestHilbertPairing_eq_zero
    {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H]
    [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]
    (testToHilbert :
      DeningerArithmeticTopologicalH1Compact →L[ℂ] H)
    (hilbertToDistribution :
      H →L[ℂ] DeningerArithmeticCompactOpenH1)
    (pairing_compatibility :
      ∀ ell x,
        ell (hilbertToDistribution x) =
          @inner ℂ H _ (testToHilbert ell) x)
    (ell : DeningerArithmeticTopologicalH1Compact)
    (x : H) :
    ell (hilbertToDistribution x) = 0 := by
  have hbase := pairing_compatibility ell x
  have hI := pairing_compatibility (Complex.I • ell) x
  simp only [map_smul, _root_.smul_apply,
    inner_smul_left, conj_I] at hI
  rw [hbase] at hI
  have hinner :
      @inner ℂ H _ (testToHilbert ell) x = 0 := by
    have htwoI : (2 * Complex.I : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by norm_num
    apply mul_left_cancel₀ htwoI
    linear_combination hI
  exact hbase.trans hinner

/--
Source-defined Gelfand triple around a Hilbert middle-cohomology completion.

`testToHilbert` is conjugate-linear with dense range, `hilbertToDistribution` is linear and
injective, and the two embeddings realize the original continuous-dual pairing as the Hilbert
pairing.  Conjugate-linearity in the test embedding is forced by mathlib's
conjugate-linear-first inner-product convention.
-/
structure DeningerArithmeticGelfandTriple
    (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H]
    [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] where
  testToHilbert :
    DeningerArithmeticTopologicalH1Compact →L⋆[ℂ] H
  hilbertToDistribution :
    H →L[ℂ] DeningerArithmeticCompactOpenH1
  test_dense : DenseRange testToHilbert
  hilbertToDistribution_injective :
    Function.Injective hilbertToDistribution
  pairing_compatibility :
    ∀ ell x,
      ell (hilbertToDistribution x) =
        @inner ℂ H _ (testToHilbert ell) x

/--
Completed Deninger middle cohomology.

The closed polarized generator is compared to the source distributional Frobenius on its full
domain.  Every source Xi eigenclass is required to have a lift in that domain.  This is the exact
completion/spectral-survival gate: neither positivity nor zero spectrum is inserted by defining
the Hilbert carrier from a divisor.
-/
structure DeningerArithmeticHilbertCohomology
    (H : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup H]
    [InnerProductSpace ℂ H] [CompleteSpace H] where
  gelfand : DeningerArithmeticGelfandTriple H
  polarization : DeningerClosedWeightOnePolarization H

radiative term vanishes by itself. -/
theorem d4GaugeFixedTeukolsky_responseJumpAntiAligned_iff_radiative_eq_zero_of_Peierls
    (pairing : X →ₗ[ℂ] Y →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ)
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (Delta : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X)
    (hB : ∀ x y, B x y = B y x)
    (hcyclic : ∀ x y z, pairing x (B y z) = pairing z (B x y))
    (hRpm : RpmRet - RpmAdv = Delta)
    (hskew : ∀ f g, d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyPeierlsSourcePairing pairing Delta f g =
      -d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyPeierlsSourcePairing pairing Delta g f) :
    pairing m (B p ((RpmRet - RpmAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusMinusResidual B p m))) =
        -pairing m (B m ((RppRet - RppAdv)
          (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p))) ↔
      pairing m (B m ((RppRet - RppAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p))) = 0 := by
  rw [hRpm, d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyPeierls_mixed_self_eq_zero pairing B Delta p m
    hB hcyclic hskew]
  constructor <;> intro h <;> linear_combination h

/-- Closed route class: source-derived cyclic Peierls incidence leaves no nontrivial
stationary/radiative cancellation mechanism in the HB causal cut. -/
def D4HBPeierlsStationaryRadiativeAntiAlignmentRouteKilled : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type) [AddCommGroup X] [Module ℂ X]
    [AddCommGroup Y] [Module ℂ Y]
    (pairing : X →ₗ[ℂ] Y →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ)
    (B : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (C : X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] X →ₗ[ℂ] Y)
    (Delta : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X)
    (RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv : Y →ₗ[ℂ] X) (p m : X),
    (∀ x y, B x y = B y x) →
    (∀ x y z, pairing x (B y z) = pairing z (B x y)) →
    RpmRet - RpmAdv = Delta →
    (∀ f g, d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyPeierlsSourcePairing pairing Delta f g =
      -d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyPeierlsSourcePairing pairing Delta g f) →
    (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCokernelCausalCut
        (pairing m) B C RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m = 0 ↔
      pairing m (B m ((RppRet - RppAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p))) = 0) ∧
    (pairing m (B p ((RpmRet - RpmAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusMinusResidual B p m))) =
        -pairing m (B m ((RppRet - RppAdv)
          (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p))) ↔
      pairing m (B m ((RppRet - RppAdv)
        (d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyQuadraticPlusPlusResidual B p))) = 0)

/-- Premise-free Lean certificate killing the physical stationary/radiative anti-alignment branch
of the HB causal-cut route. -/
theorem d4HBPeierlsStationaryRadiativeAntiAlignmentRouteKilled :
    D4HBPeierlsStationaryRadiativeAntiAlignmentRouteKilled := by
  intro X Y _ _ _ _ pairing B C Delta RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m
    hB hcyclic hRpm hskew
  exact ⟨
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolskyTotalPlusPlusMinusCokernelCausalCut_eq_zero_iff_radiative_of_Peierls
      pairing B C Delta RppRet RpmRet RppAdv RpmAdv p m hB hcyclic hRpm hskew,
    d4GaugeFixedTeukolsky_responseJumpAntiAligned_iff_radiative_eq_zero_of_Peierls
